title: POLYNURSE - FOUNDATION OF NURSING - TOURNAMENT POOL (500 questions, all Hard-targeted)

questions.question: A nurse removes the needle after a radial arterial blood gas on a client taking warfarin. How long should firm pressure be applied?

options.A: 1 minute
options.B: 2 minutes
options.C: At least 10 minutes
options.D: 5 minutes

questions.correct_text: At least 10 minutes
explanation: A longer time is needed in clients on anticoagulants to prevent a hematoma and bleeding from the artery.
Five minutes is the usual time without anticoagulation.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with angina teaches back instructions for sublingual nitroglycerin. Which statement shows correct understanding?

options.A: I will take up to 3 tablets over 30 minutes before I decide whether to call 911 today
options.B: I will keep the tablets in a weekly pill organizer for easy access each day
options.C: I will swallow the tablet with a full glass of water so that it works quickly
options.D: If pain persists 5 minutes after the first tablet, I will call emergency services

questions.correct_text: If pain persists 5 minutes after the first tablet, I will call emergency services
explanation: Pain that persists 5 minutes after one dose may mean a heart attack, so emergency services are called.
Tablets are dissolved under the tongue and kept in the original dark glass container.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client who usually weighs 60 kg has lost 10% of body weight from vomiting and diarrhea. The provider orders replacement of half the deficit over 8 hours. At what rate in mL/hr should the pump be set? (1 kg is about 1 L.)

options.A: 750 mL/hr
options.B: 250 mL/hr
options.C: 375 mL/hr
options.D: 188 mL/hr

questions.correct_text: 375 mL/hr
explanation: Deficit: 10% of 60 kg = 6 kg, or about 6,000 mL.
750 mL/hr results from replacing the full deficit in 8 hours.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with small cell lung cancer has a sodium of 121 mEq/L, low serum osmolality, concentrated urine, weight gain without edema, headache, and mild confusion. What should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: An infusion of 5% dextrose in water
options.B: A 1,000 mL bolus of 0.9% sodium chloride
options.C: Encouraging oral fluids to 3 liters daily at this time
options.D: Fluid restriction and close neurologic monitoring

questions.correct_text: Fluid restriction and close neurologic monitoring
explanation: The findings suggest water retention from excess antidiuretic hormone, which dilutes the sodium.
Extra fluid, including free water, worsens the dilution and brain swelling.
Restriction raises the sodium gradually and safely.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A nurse has drawn up part of a single-dose vial and wants to use the rest for the next client. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Use the vial after wiping the top with alcohol
options.B: Discard the vial and use a new one for the next client
options.C: Use the vial for the next client with a new needle as planned
options.D: Label the vial and store it for 24 hours

questions.correct_text: Discard the vial and use a new one for the next client
explanation: A single-dose vial has no preservative and is discarded after one use.
Reusing it can spread infection between clients.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with a T4 spinal cord injury suddenly has a pounding headache, a flushed face and neck, sweating above the injury, BP 214/118, and HR 54. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Sit the client upright, loosen tight clothing, and check bladder and bowel
options.B: Give the PRN analgesic for the headache and recheck the pressure in 30 minutes
options.C: Apply a heating pad to the lower abdomen to relax the bladder muscles
options.D: Lay the client flat, raise the legs, and give a fluid bolus right away

questions.correct_text: Sit the client upright, loosen tight clothing, and check bladder and bowel
explanation: A trigger below the injury, often a full bladder or bowel, causes an uncontrolled surge in pressure.
Sitting upright lowers pressure, and removing the trigger stops the reflex.
Lying flat raises pressure further.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: An older client has taken opioids for 5 days with no formed stool for 6 days. The client reports cramping, leaks small amounts of liquid stool, and has a distended abdomen. A PRN loperamide order is available. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Give an additional dose of the opioid for cramping
options.B: Give the loperamide to stop the diarrhea
options.C: Hold the loperamide and assess for stool impaction
options.D: Encourage fluids and monitor the stools

questions.correct_text: Hold the loperamide and assess for stool impaction
explanation: Liquid stool leaking around a hard mass is overflow from impaction.
An antidiarrheal worsens the blockage and risks obstruction.
Assessment and a plan to remove the impaction come first.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: During a transfusion, the nurse rechecks the unit and finds that the blood type on the bag does not match the client's record. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Complete the transfusion and document the discrepancy
options.B: Stop the transfusion, keep the IV open with saline through new tubing, and check vital signs
options.C: Return the unit and restart a new one with the same tubing today as planned
options.D: Slow the transfusion and recheck in 15 minutes

questions.correct_text: Stop the transfusion, keep the IV open with saline through new tubing, and check vital signs
explanation: A mismatch can cause fatal hemolysis, and every minute adds exposure.
The client is assessed, and the blood bank and provider are told.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: The RN is assigning four clients. Which client is most appropriate to assign to the LPN/LVN?

options.A: A client who needs discharge teaching on a new insulin regimen and glucose monitoring
options.B: A client admitted this morning who needs an initial admission assessment and care plan
options.C: A client with new chest pain who needs ongoing evaluation of ECG changes and troponin results
options.D: A stable client on postoperative day 3 needing a sterile dressing change and oral medications

questions.correct_text: A stable client on postoperative day 3 needing a sterile dressing change and oral medications
explanation: LPNs care for stable clients with predictable outcomes and perform focused data collection and skills.
Initial assessment, care planning, and teaching new content stay with the RN, as does evaluating unstable changes.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Twenty minutes after a right subclavian central line insertion, a client develops sudden dyspnea, SpO2 80%, absent breath sounds on the right, a tracheal shift to the left, BP 78/50, and distended neck veins. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Obtain a portable chest x-ray first and confirm before any treatment
options.B: Apply oxygen by mask and reassess the client's breathing in 15 minutes
options.C: Prepare for immediate needle decompression and call a rapid response
options.D: Remove the central line and observe the client's breathing closely

questions.correct_text: Prepare for immediate needle decompression and call a rapid response
explanation: The findings indicate air trapped under pressure, which shifts the mediastinum and blocks venous return.
Treatment is immediate and does not wait for imaging.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Tension pneumothorax after a central line

questions.question: A client with heart failure has diminished breath sounds, dullness to percussion, and decreased tactile fremitus over the left lower chest. What do these findings suggest?

options.A: A pneumothorax
options.B: A pleural effusion
options.C: Bronchospasm
options.D: Pneumonia with consolidation

questions.correct_text: A pleural effusion
explanation: Fluid between the lung and chest wall blocks sound and gives a dull percussion note.
Consolidation raises fremitus, and a pneumothorax gives a hyperresonant note.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with a sealed internal radiation implant for cervical cancer has a radioactive source found in the bed linens. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Use long-handled forceps to place the source in the lead container and call radiation safety
options.B: Leave the source in place, move the client to another room, and close the door until morning
options.C: Wrap the source in the linens and send them to the laundry with a warning label for staff
options.D: Pick it up quickly with double gloves and place it in the lead-lined container for disposal

questions.correct_text: Use long-handled forceps to place the source in the lead container and call radiation safety
explanation: Distance is a key protection, so a sealed source is never touched by hand and long-handled forceps are used.
The source must be contained in the lead container and the radiation safety officer notified.
Gloves do not block radiation, and sending it to laundry or leaving it loose exposes others.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A nurse finds a client on the floor beside the bed. Which documentation entry is best?

options.A: "0215: Client appears to be confused and probably wanted to get out of bed." right now
options.B: "0215: Found on floor beside bed. Client states, 'I slid down.' No visible injury. BP 138/82, HR 84. Provider notified 0220."
options.C: "0215: Client fell after staff were slow to answer the call light."
options.D: "0215: Client tripped over his own feet. An incident report was filed."

questions.correct_text: "0215: Found on floor beside bed. Client states, 'I slid down.' No visible injury. BP 138/82, HR 84. Provider notified 0220."
explanation: Notes state facts and the client's words and do not assign blame or guess.
The incident report is a separate document and is not mentioned in the chart.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Which postoperative client should the nurse see first?

options.A: A client 4 hours after thyroidectomy with neck swelling, noisy breathing, and SpO2 93%
options.B: A client after knee replacement who reports pain of 8/10 and requests the PRN opioid
options.C: A client after hernia repair who has voided 150 mL and asks to go home
options.D: A client after cholecystectomy who feels nauseated and has been unable to eat for 12 hours

questions.correct_text: A client 4 hours after thyroidectomy with neck swelling, noisy breathing, and SpO2 93%
explanation: Swelling around the neck with noisy breathing suggests bleeding or edema compressing the airway.
The other clients have needs that matter but are not threatening the airway.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with a suspected pelvic fracture is hypotensive. Which action is correct?

options.A: Have the client sit up and walk to the stretcher at this time
options.B: Rock the pelvis to test the stability
options.C: Apply a pelvic binder and avoid rocking the pelvis
options.D: Roll the client repeatedly to inspect the back

questions.correct_text: Apply a pelvic binder and avoid rocking the pelvis
explanation: Movement can disrupt clots and increase bleeding.
A binder stabilizes the pelvis and limits bleeding.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A worker has heavy sweating, a temperature of 39.0 C, headache, nausea, and weakness, and is fully oriented. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Withhold fluids until the temperature falls
options.B: Move the worker to a cool place, remove excess clothing, and give cool fluids by mouth while monitoring mental status
options.C: Give acetaminophen and send the worker back to work as planned
options.D: Apply warm blankets to prevent shivering

questions.correct_text: Move the worker to a cool place, remove excess clothing, and give cool fluids by mouth while monitoring mental status
explanation: Sweating, a normal mental state, and a temperature below about 40 C fit heat exhaustion.
A change in mental status would signal heat stroke, which needs aggressive cooling.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client in the recovery room after hip surgery has BP 80/40, HR 120, and cool skin. The dressing is dry, and the drain holds just 20 mL. The operative thigh looks larger than before today. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Anesthesia effect that will resolve without action
options.B: Dehydration that needs oral fluids once the client is awake
options.C: Concealed bleeding into the thigh, so the nurse measures the thigh and reports the changes
options.D: Pain alone, so the nurse gives an analgesic and rechecks the pressure right now for the moment

questions.correct_text: Concealed bleeding into the thigh, so the nurse measures the thigh and reports the changes
explanation: A dry dressing with a swollen limb, low pressure, and a fast pulse suggests bleeding into the tissue.
Low drainage does not rule out blood loss.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with an epidural infusion for pain received enoxaparin 6 hours ago. The client now reports new severe back pain, leg numbness, and weakness in both legs. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Document the findings carefully and reassess the client in 1 hour
options.B: Stop the epidural infusion and perform a neurologic check
options.C: Help the client turn to the side and apply a heating pad
options.D: Increase the infusion rate to relieve the new back pain

questions.correct_text: Stop the epidural infusion and perform a neurologic check
explanation: New back pain with leg weakness after an epidural plus an anticoagulant suggests bleeding around the spinal cord.
Stopping the infusion allows neurologic checks, and rapid imaging and decompression save function.
More local anesthetic or a delay hides and worsens the injury.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Four hours after surgery, a client has BP 118/84, HR 108, RR 22, cool skin, and anxiety. Two hours ago the BP was 130/70 and HR 84. How should the nurse interpret these findings?

options.A: Pain response that will settle with the next analgesic dose at this time
options.B: Fluid overload from IV therapy
options.C: Expected recovery from anesthesia
options.D: Early compensated blood loss with a narrowing pulse pressure

questions.correct_text: Early compensated blood loss with a narrowing pulse pressure
explanation: Pulse pressure narrowed from 60 to 34, and heart rate rose, while systolic BP is still normal.
Cool skin and anxiety reflect compensation for lost volume.
Falling blood pressure is a late sign and should not be awaited.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has fever and a productive cough. Over the right lower lobe, the nurse hears loud, tubular breath sounds, with dull percussion and increased tactile fremitus. What do these findings suggest?

options.A: Emphysema
options.B: Pneumothorax
options.C: Consolidation from pneumonia
options.D: A pleural effusion

questions.correct_text: Consolidation from pneumonia
explanation: Solid lung transmits sound well, which gives bronchial breath sounds and increased fremitus with dullness.
Fluid in the pleural space and air in the pleural space reduce sound transmission.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: During a cranial nerve assessment, a client's tongue deviates to the left when protruded. What does this suggest?

options.A: A right hypoglossal nerve deficit
options.B: A left hypoglossal nerve (cranial nerve XII) deficit
options.C: A glossopharyngeal nerve deficit
options.D: An abnormal vagus nerve response

questions.correct_text: A left hypoglossal nerve (cranial nerve XII) deficit
explanation: The tongue deviates toward the side of the weak nerve.
Cranial nerve XII controls tongue movement.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client taking gentamicin and ibuprofen has creatinine values of 0.9, 1.4, and 1.9 mg/dL over 24 hours and a urine output of 15 mL/hr. What should the nurse conclude?

options.A: Dehydration that needs oral fluids alone
options.B: A normal response to infection that needs no change in therapy
options.C: An expected change with age that can be rechecked in 3 days
options.D: Acute kidney injury, so nephrotoxic drugs should be held per protocol and the findings reported

questions.correct_text: Acute kidney injury, so nephrotoxic drugs should be held per protocol and the findings reported
explanation: A fast rise in creatinine with low urine output signals acute injury to the kidneys.
Aminoglycosides and NSAIDs both harm the kidneys.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has just had a percutaneous liver biopsy. Which position is correct?

options.A: Lying on the right side with a pillow under the costal margin for several hours
options.B: Sitting upright to ease the breathing
options.C: Lying on the back with the legs bent and a sandbag on the abdomen at this time for the moment
options.D: Lying on the left side with the head of the bed flat

questions.correct_text: Lying on the right side with a pillow under the costal margin for several hours
explanation: Pressure on the puncture site from the client's own weight helps prevent bleeding.
Vital signs and bleeding signs are monitored closely.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Before a radial ABG on a client taking warfarin, the nurse performs a modified Allen test. After releasing pressure on the ulnar artery, the hand stays pale for 12 seconds. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Proceed and hold pressure for 10 minutes afterward
options.B: Avoid that radial artery and assess the other wrist
options.C: Proceed using a smaller-gauge needle
options.D: Repeat the test while the client keeps the fist closed

questions.correct_text: Avoid that radial artery and assess the other wrist
explanation: Color should return within about 5 to 10 seconds if the ulnar artery can supply the hand.
A delay shows poor collateral flow, so radial puncture risks hand ischemia.
Longer pressure or a smaller needle does not fix inadequate collateral flow.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client's left ventricle holds 100 mL at the end of filling and ejects 30 mL with each beat. What is the ejection fraction, and what does it indicate?

options.A: 30%, a reduced value that suggests weak pumping
options.B: 70%, a reduced value
options.C: 30%, a normal value
options.D: 3.3%, a normal value

questions.correct_text: 30%, a reduced value that suggests weak pumping
explanation: Ejection fraction = stroke volume / end-diastolic volume = 30 / 100.
A normal value is about 55% to 70%.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Order: magnesium sulfate 4 g IV over 20 minutes. The pharmacy sends 4 g in 100 mL. What rate in mL/hr should the nurse set?

options.A: 200 mL/hr
options.B: 120 mL/hr
options.C: 100 mL/hr
options.D: 300 mL/hr

questions.correct_text: 300 mL/hr
explanation: 100 mL in 20 minutes is 5 mL/min.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: An IV bag of 500 mL is started at 0930 and runs at 85 mL/hr. At what time will the infusion finish?
explanation: 500 / 85 = 5.88 hours, or 5 hours 53 minutes.
0930 plus 5 hours 53 minutes is 1523.
1553 comes from rounding the time up to 6 hours.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with multiple sclerosis reports that weakness and blurred vision worsen after a hot bath. What should the nurse teach?

options.A: Cold water should be avoided in every situation
options.B: The symptoms show that the disease has become permanently worse
options.C: Hot baths strengthen the muscles and should continue
options.D: Heat can temporarily worsen symptoms, so use cool or lukewarm water and avoid overheating

questions.correct_text: Heat can temporarily worsen symptoms, so use cool or lukewarm water and avoid overheating
explanation: A small rise in body temperature slows nerve conduction in damaged nerves.
The symptoms usually return to baseline after cooling.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A child weighs 14 kg. Using 100 mL/kg for the first 10 kg and 50 mL/kg for the next kilograms, what is the maintenance fluid per hour? (Round to the nearest whole number.)

options.A: 58 mL/hr
options.B: 1,400 mL/hr
options.C: 50 mL/hr
options.D: 25 mL/hr

questions.correct_text: 50 mL/hr
explanation: First 10 kg: 1,000 mL; next 4 kg: 200 mL; total 1,200 mL per day.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client on day 1 after a lumbar fusion needs a linen change. Which technique is correct?

options.A: Ask the client to twist the shoulders and then the hips to roll over
options.B: Have one nurse pull the client to the side by the arm and leg
options.C: Raise the head of the bed to 90 degrees and pivot the client to the chair today right now
options.D: Log roll with a turning sheet and at least two staff, keeping the spine aligned with a pillow between the knees

questions.correct_text: Log roll with a turning sheet and at least two staff, keeping the spine aligned with a pillow between the knees
explanation: The spine must move as one unit, so the body turns together.
Twisting or uneven pulling can injure the surgical site and spinal cord.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client uses an insulin-to-carbohydrate ratio of 1 unit per 10 g and a correction factor of 1 unit for each 50 mg/dL above 150. The glucose is 250 mg/dL, and the meal has 75 g of carbohydrate. How many units should the client receive?

options.A: 9.5 units
options.B: 11.5 units
options.C: 2 units
options.D: 7.5 units

questions.correct_text: 9.5 units
explanation: Meal dose: 75 / 10 = 7.5 units.
Correction dose: (250 - 150) / 50 = 2 units.
Total 7.5 + 2 = 9.5 units.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A burned adult weighs 70 kg and has 36% total body surface area burned. Using the Parkland formula (4 mL x kg x % burned), how many mL should be given in the first 8 hours?

options.B: 630 mL

explanation: Total for 24 hours is 4 x 70 x 36 = 10,080 mL.
Half is given in the first 8 hours after the burn, which is 5,040 mL.
630 mL is the hourly rate during that time.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: An older client with advanced dementia cannot report pain. After a hip fracture repair, the nurse observes grimacing, moaning, restlessness, and guarding. Vital signs are normal. What should the nurse conclude?

options.A: Pain cannot be treated until the client is able to rate it on a numeric scale
options.B: Pain is unlikely when vital signs are normal and the client makes no verbal complaint
options.C: Anxiety is the likely cause and a low-dose sedative should be tried before analgesics
options.D: Pain is likely and should be treated based on behavior, even with normal vital signs

questions.correct_text: Pain is likely and should be treated based on behavior, even with normal vital signs
explanation: Behavior is a valid pain indicator when self-report is not possible, and a behavioral scale guides treatment.
Vital signs often stay normal in chronic or ongoing pain.
A sedative can mask pain and increase the risk of delirium and falls.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A child weighs 18 kg and is NPO. Using the 4-2-1 rule, what maintenance IV rate in mL/hr is correct?

options.A: 56 mL/hr
options.B: 36 mL/hr
options.C: 72 mL/hr
options.D: 68 mL/hr

questions.correct_text: 56 mL/hr
explanation: First 10 kg: 10 x 4 = 40 mL/hr.
Next 8 kg: 8 x 2 = 16 mL/hr; total 56 mL/hr.
72 applies 4 mL/kg to the whole weight; 36 applies 2 mL/kg to the whole weight.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: After large-volume resuscitation with 0.9% sodium chloride (6 liters), a client has sodium 144, chloride 118, bicarbonate 16, and an anion gap of 10. Which cause is most likely?

options.A: Ketoacidosis from starvation
options.B: Lactic acidosis from shock
options.C: Respiratory acidosis from hypoventilation today for now
options.D: Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis from the saline

questions.correct_text: Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis from the saline
explanation: Chloride-rich saline lowers bicarbonate and produces a normal-gap acidosis.
A normal gap rules out added acids such as lactate or ketones.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Four hours after a colonoscopy with polyp removal, a client has severe abdominal pain, a rigid abdomen, a temperature of 38.3 C, and HR 112. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Apply a heating pad and observe
options.B: Give a gas-relieving medication and encourage walking at this time as planned
options.C: Keep the client NPO and monitor the vital signs and abdomen closely
options.D: Offer clear liquids and recheck in an hour

questions.correct_text: Keep the client NPO and monitor the vital signs and abdomen closely
explanation: Severe pain, rigidity, and fever after the procedure suggest a hole in the bowel.
Food and heat are unsafe.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: After a car crash, a client has a section of the chest wall that moves inward on inspiration and outward on expiration. The client reports severe pain, and SpO2 is 86%. What should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Oxygen, pain control, and preparation for ventilatory support
options.B: Lying flat with a heavy sandbag on the chest
options.C: Vigorous coughing and deep breathing without pain relief for now
options.D: Tight taping of the chest wall

questions.correct_text: Oxygen, pain control, and preparation for ventilatory support
explanation: Opposite movement of the chest segment impairs breathing, and pain adds to the problem.
The client may need a ventilator to stabilize the chest from within.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: During CPR on an adult with an advanced airway in place, which action by a team member requires correction?

options.A: Compressing at about 110 per minute
options.B: Delivering 2 breaths after every 30 compressions
options.C: Allowing full chest recoil between compressions at this time
options.D: Switching compressors about every 2 minutes

questions.correct_text: Delivering 2 breaths after every 30 compressions
explanation: With an advanced airway, compressions are continuous and one breath is given about every 6 seconds.
Pausing for paired breaths lowers coronary perfusion.
The rate, rotation, and recoil described are correct.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A nurse inserts a nasogastric tube in an unconscious client who cannot swallow on command. Which technique improves the chance of correct placement?

options.A: Flex the head forward, chin toward chest, as the tube passes the throat
options.B: Advance the tube rapidly in one smooth motion to reduce gagging and time
options.C: Place the client flat with the head hyperextended to straighten the airway
options.D: Ask the client to swallow small sips of water as the tube advances down

questions.correct_text: Flex the head forward, chin toward chest, as the tube passes the throat
explanation: Flexing the head closes the trachea and directs the tube into the esophagus.
An unconscious client cannot swallow on command, and water given to the client risks aspiration.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Nasogastric insertion in an unconscious client

questions.question: A client with a central venous catheter has a temperature of 39.6 C and chills 30 minutes after the line was flushed. The insertion site looks clean. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Remove the line at once and send the tip for culture
options.B: Start the antibiotic through the line before drawing cultures at this time today today
options.C: Give acetaminophen and recheck the temperature in 4 hours
options.D: Obtain blood cultures from the line and from a peripheral site before antibiotics

questions.correct_text: Obtain blood cultures from the line and from a peripheral site before antibiotics
explanation: Fever and chills after line access suggest a bloodstream infection from the catheter.
Cultures come first so that the organism can be identified, and antibiotics follow without delay.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Fever after a central line flush

questions.question: A client on a ventilator has pH 7.50, PaCO2 28 mm Hg, and HCO3 24 mEq/L. What does the nurse conclude?

options.A: Respiratory alkalosis from overventilation, and the settings need review
options.B: A normal result for a client on a ventilator
options.C: Metabolic alkalosis from vomiting
options.D: Respiratory acidosis from undertreatment

questions.correct_text: Respiratory alkalosis from overventilation, and the settings need review
explanation: A low PaCO2 with a high pH means too much carbon dioxide is being blown off.
The rate or tidal volume may need to be lowered by the provider or respiratory therapist.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client opens the eyes to painful stimulus alone, makes incomprehensible sounds, and withdraws from pain. What is the Glasgow Coma Scale score and its most important implication?

options.A: Score 7; the client has a normal level of arousal
options.B: Score 10; the client can protect the airway
options.C: Score 8; airway protection may be inadequate
options.D: Score 9; the client needs routine neurologic checks every hour

questions.correct_text: Score 8; airway protection may be inadequate
explanation: Eyes to pain score 2, incomprehensible sounds score 2, and withdrawal scores 4, giving 8.
A score of 8 or less signals severe impairment and a high risk of airway compromise.
Other totals result from scoring a component too high or too low.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Order: dopamine 5 mcg/kg/min. The client weighs 70 kg. The bag contains dopamine 400 mg in 250 mL. What pump rate in mL/hr should the nurse set? (Round to the nearest tenth.)

options.A: 131.3 mL/hr
options.B: 1.3 mL/hr
options.C: 21.9 mL/hr
options.D: 13.1 mL/hr

questions.correct_text: 13.1 mL/hr
explanation: Dose: 5 x 70 = 350 mcg/min = 21,000 mcg/hr.
Concentration: 400,000 mcg / 250 mL = 1,600 mcg/mL.
21,000 / 1,600 = 13.1 mL/hr; the other values reflect decimal or unit errors.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client using BiPAP for respiratory failure becomes nauseated, drowsy, and begins to vomit. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Raise the head of the bed and leave the mask in place
options.B: Remove the mask and suction the airway
options.C: Tighten the mask straps to stop air leaking
options.D: Lower the pressure settings and keep the mask on

questions.correct_text: Remove the mask and suction the airway
explanation: The mask traps vomit over the nose and mouth, and a drowsy client is at high risk of aspiration.
The airway is cleared first, and the need for intubation is then reassessed.
Adjusting pressure or position with the mask on does not protect the airway.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has a heart rate of 90/min and a stroke volume of 55 mL. What is the cardiac output?

options.A: 145 L/min
options.B: 49.5 L/min
options.C: 0.61 L/min
options.D: 4.95 L/min

questions.correct_text: 4.95 L/min
explanation: Cardiac output = heart rate x stroke volume = 90 x 55 = 4,950 mL/min.
This equals about 5 L/min.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with a shellfish allergy is scheduled for a CT scan with iodinated contrast. The client has no history of prior contrast. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Document the allergy and ask about prior contrast reactions and other allergies
options.B: Tell the client that the contrast dye is made from shellfish proteins and iodine
options.C: Proceed without extra screening, as the risk is the same as for other clients
options.D: Cancel the scan, as a shellfish allergy is a contraindication to contrast dye

questions.correct_text: Document the allergy and ask about prior contrast reactions and other allergies
explanation: Shellfish allergy does not reliably predict contrast reactions, but a history of allergy still raises the risk and is reported.
Past reactions to contrast are the most useful screening information.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with type 2 diabetes finishes eating an orange and has a fingerstick glucose of 486 mg/dL. The client has no symptoms, and the morning glucose was 148. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Wipe the same finger with an alcohol swab, allow to dry, and repeat the test
options.B: Give the prescribed correction dose of rapid-acting insulin per the sliding scale
options.C: Send a venous glucose to the laboratory and hold the lunch tray until it returns
options.D: Wash the client's hands with soap and water, then retest on a different finger

questions.correct_text: Wash the client's hands with soap and water, then retest on a different finger
explanation: Fruit sugar on the fingertip can give a falsely high reading.
Treating an unverified value risks hypoglycemia, and alcohol residue can also alter results.
Washing and retesting a different site is quick and avoids unnecessary treatment.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client on postoperative day 2 after a colostomy and midline incision needs help walking. Where should the nurse place the gait belt?

options.A: Around the waist, positioned to avoid the stoma and incision, with the nurse's hands on the belt
options.B: Loosely around the chest under the arms, with the pouch tucked under the belt
options.C: Directly over the pouch and stoma so that the client can hold the belt in place right now
options.D: Over the dressing so the incision is held firmly while the client walks

questions.correct_text: Around the waist, positioned to avoid the stoma and incision, with the nurse's hands on the belt
explanation: A belt over a stoma or fresh incision creates pressure and can injure the tissue or pull the pouch off.
The belt is placed to give a secure grip while protecting both sites.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Gait belt with an abdominal stoma

questions.question: A client clearly refuses an injection, and the nurse gives it anyway. Which legal term best describes the act?

options.A: Assault, a threat made without any contact
options.B: Libel, a false written statement
options.C: Battery, the touching of a person without consent
options.D: Defamation, a false harm to reputation

questions.correct_text: Battery, the touching of a person without consent
explanation: Contact without consent is battery, even when the act is meant to help.
The nurse respects a competent client's refusal and documents it.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client opens the eyes to voice but cannot keep eye contact, and the eyes stay open less than 10 seconds each time. Using the Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale, what is the score?

options.A: 0, alert and calm
options.B: +2, agitated
options.C: -4, deep sedation
options.D: -2, light sedation

questions.correct_text: -2, light sedation
explanation: Brief awakening with eye contact for less than 10 seconds to voice is a score of -2.
A score of -3 involves movement or eye opening to voice without eye contact.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: An older adult with type 2 diabetes has a glucose of 880 mg/dL, no ketones, a sodium of 150 mEq/L, and confusion. What should the nurse anticipate first?

options.A: Aggressive isotonic IV fluids
options.B: A rapid IV insulin bolus alone
options.C: Oral fluids as tolerated
options.D: A bicarbonate infusion

questions.correct_text: Aggressive isotonic IV fluids
explanation: The picture fits a hyperosmolar state with severe dehydration.
Fluids come first, and insulin follows once volume is restored.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client needs 1,800 kcal daily from a formula that provides 1.5 kcal/mL. At what continuous rate in mL/hr over 24 hours should the feeding run?

options.A: 75 mL/hr
options.B: 34 mL/hr
options.C: 50 mL/hr
options.D: 120 mL/hr

questions.correct_text: 50 mL/hr
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A meal contains 40 g of protein, 60 g of carbohydrate, and 20 g of fat. Protein and carbohydrate provide 4 kcal/g and fat provides 9 kcal/g. How many kilocalories does the meal provide?

options.A: 580 kcal
options.B: 760 kcal
options.C: 120 kcal
options.D: 540 kcal

questions.correct_text: 580 kcal
explanation: Protein: 40 x 4 = 160; carbohydrate: 60 x 4 = 240; fat: 20 x 9 = 180.
The total is 580 kcal.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Order: propofol 25 mcg/kg/min. The client weighs 80 kg, and the concentration is 10 mg/mL. What rate in mL/hr should the nurse set?

options.A: 120 mL/hr
options.B: 12 mL/hr
options.C: 2 mL/hr
options.D: 7.5 mL/hr

questions.correct_text: 12 mL/hr
explanation: 25 x 80 = 2,000 mcg/min = 2 mg/min.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A heparin bag contains 25,000 units in 250 mL. The pump is running at 12 mL/hr, and the client weighs 80 kg. What dose is the client receiving?

options.A: 15 units/kg/hr
options.B: 19 units/kg/hr
options.C: 12 units/kg/hr
options.D: 150 units/kg/hr

questions.correct_text: 15 units/kg/hr
explanation: Concentration: 25,000 / 250 = 100 units/mL.
12 mL/hr x 100 = 1,200 units/hr; 1,200 / 80 = 15 units/kg/hr.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Heparin dose from the pump rate

questions.question: A 68-year-old with dyspnea, bibasilar crackles, and ankle edema has an extra heart sound heard early in diastole, soon after S2, best at the apex. What does this finding suggest?

options.A: A normal split of S2, expected in many older adults at rest
options.B: An S4 sound, indicating a stiff and noncompliant ventricle
options.C: A pericardial friction rub, heard with inflammation of the sac
options.D: An S3 sound, indicating volume overload and ventricular failure

questions.correct_text: An S3 sound, indicating volume overload and ventricular failure
explanation: An S3 follows S2 in early diastole and reflects rapid filling of an overloaded ventricle.
An S4 comes just before S1, and a friction rub is a scratchy sound heard in both phases.
With dyspnea, crackles, and edema, an S3 supports heart failure.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Which client should the nurse see first?

options.A: A client on postoperative day 2 with a temperature of 37.9 C and a productive cough
options.B: A client on postoperative day 2 with sudden sharp chest pain on inspiration, SpO2 91%, and HR 118
options.C: A client on postoperative day 2 with incisional pain of 7/10 that eases after the last analgesic
options.D: A client on postoperative day 2 with a red, warm calf that has been swollen for the past day

questions.correct_text: A client on postoperative day 2 with sudden sharp chest pain on inspiration, SpO2 91%, and HR 118
explanation: Sudden chest pain with hypoxemia and tachycardia suggests a clot in the lung.
A swollen calf needs attention, but the client with a possible lung clot is less stable.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client received acetaminophen 650 mg at 0000, 0400, 0800, and 1200, and one tablet of hydrocodone 5 mg/acetaminophen 325 mg at 0200, 0600, 1000, and 1400. At 1600 the client requests the next 650 mg dose for pain. The daily maximum is 4,000 mg. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Give half of the 650 mg dose to keep the daily total under 4,000 mg and chart it
options.B: Give the dose now and report the running total at the end of the shift
options.C: Give the dose, as 4 hours have elapsed after the last acetaminophen dose
options.D: Hold the dose and seek another analgesic option; the total would exceed 4,000 mg

questions.correct_text: Hold the dose and seek another analgesic option; the total would exceed 4,000 mg
explanation: Acetaminophen already given totals 2,600 + 1,300 = 3,900 mg in 16 hours, and another 650 mg would reach 4,550 mg.
Combination opioids contain hidden acetaminophen that must be counted.
Altering the dose without an order is outside nursing practice.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has a stage 3 pressure injury with purulent, foul-smelling drainage. Four dressing plans are written. Which plan should the nurse question?

options.A: Calcium alginate with a secondary cover dressing
options.B: A hydrocolloid dressing left in place for 5 days
options.C: A silver-impregnated foam dressing changed daily
options.D: Moist saline gauze changed twice daily

questions.correct_text: A hydrocolloid dressing left in place for 5 days
explanation: An occlusive hydrocolloid traps bacteria and moisture, which can worsen infection and prevents daily inspection.
Alginate, silver foam, and moist gauze manage exudate or bacteria and allow frequent assessment.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Dressing choice for an infected wound

questions.question: A client receiving peritoneal dialysis has cloudy outflow fluid, abdominal pain, and a temperature of 38.4 C. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Irrigate the catheter with saline
options.B: Give acetaminophen and continue the exchange
options.C: Clamp the catheter and wait for the fluid to clear as planned for the moment
options.D: Send a sample of the fluid for culture

questions.correct_text: Send a sample of the fluid for culture
explanation: Cloudy fluid with pain and fever suggests peritonitis from the dialysis catheter.
Cultures identify the organism so treatment can start.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client receiving a heparin infusion has an aPTT of 148 seconds, blood in the urine, and a falling BP. After the infusion is stopped, which drug should the nurse prepare?

options.A: Vitamin K
options.B: Flumazenil
options.C: Protamine sulfate
options.D: Digoxin immune fab

questions.correct_text: Protamine sulfate
explanation: Protamine binds heparin and reverses its effect.
Vitamin K works on warfarin and is too slow for heparin.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has four rib fractures and an SpO2 of 91%. Which order should the nurse question?

options.A: Scheduled analgesia before the breathing exercises
options.B: Position of comfort with the head of the bed elevated
options.C: Incentive spirometry with splinting every hour while awake
options.D: Chest physiotherapy with percussion every 4 hours

questions.correct_text: Chest physiotherapy with percussion every 4 hours
explanation: Percussion over fractured ribs causes severe pain and can worsen injury.
The other orders promote lung expansion with pain control.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client receives 2,000 mL of 5% dextrose in water over 24 hours. Dextrose provides 3.4 kcal/g. How many kilocalories does the client receive?

options.A: 1,700 kcal
options.B: 340 kcal
options.C: 170 kcal
options.D: 400 kcal

questions.correct_text: 340 kcal
explanation: 5% means 5 g per 100 mL, so 2,000 mL has 100 g of dextrose.
100 g x 3.4 kcal/g = 340 kcal.
400 uses 4 kcal/g, and 170 is the amount in 1,000 mL.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client rescued from a house fire has severe lactic acidosis, a drop in blood pressure, and a high level of cyanide. Which drug should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Hydroxocobalamin
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Protamine sulfate
options.D: Naloxone

questions.correct_text: Hydroxocobalamin
explanation: Hydroxocobalamin binds cyanide and forms a harmless compound.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has a triple-lumen central line, and one lumen carries continuous parenteral nutrition. The nurse needs to draw blood and give an antibiotic. Which action is correct?

options.A: Piggyback the antibiotic into the nutrition line
options.B: Use a different lumen for the blood draw and the antibiotic, and keep the nutrition lumen untouched
options.C: Flush the nutrition lumen with saline before and after each access right now at this time
options.D: Pause the nutrition and draw blood from that lumen

questions.correct_text: Use a different lumen for the blood draw and the antibiotic, and keep the nutrition lumen untouched
explanation: The nutrition lumen is kept for the solution alone, since access raises the risks of infection and incompatibility.
A separate lumen allows the other tasks.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Drawing blood from a parenteral nutrition line

questions.question: A client receiving tube feedings has a sodium of 156 mEq/L, dry mucous membranes, and low urine output. What should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: A faster formula rate to meet the client's calorie and protein needs
options.B: Salt added to the formula to replace the client's sodium losses
options.C: More free water flushes and close sodium monitoring
options.D: Free water restriction to lower the total body fluid and swelling

questions.correct_text: More free water flushes and close sodium monitoring
explanation: A client who is not able to drink loses water, and concentrated formula raises sodium further.
Added water corrects the deficit gradually.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client receiving morphine through a PCA pump is on oxygen at 3 L/min. SpO2 is 97%, respiratory rate is 6/min, and the client is hard to arouse. What does the nurse conclude?

options.A: The saturation shows that breathing is adequate and no action is needed at present
options.B: Hold the next PCA dose and reassess the sedation level and respiratory rate in an hour at this time
options.C: Increase the oxygen flow and recheck the saturation and respiratory rate in an hour
options.D: Respiratory depression is likely despite the saturation; stimulate and prepare naloxone

questions.correct_text: Respiratory depression is likely despite the saturation; stimulate and prepare naloxone
explanation: Oxygen keeps the saturation high even when breathing is dangerously slow, so rate and alertness are the better signs.
Delay can lead to respiratory arrest.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with severe malnutrition who has eaten little for 3 weeks is about to start parenteral nutrition. The pharmacy sent a bag programmed for the full goal rate. Which plan best prevents the major complication of starting nutrition?

options.A: Withhold phosphate and potassium replacement until the goal rate has been reached right now
options.B: Check electrolytes once on day 3, after the goal rate has been reached
options.C: Give thiamine, then advance the feeding gradually with frequent electrolyte checks
options.D: Start at the full goal rate to reverse the catabolic state as quickly as possible

questions.correct_text: Give thiamine, then advance the feeding gradually with frequent electrolyte checks
explanation: A sudden carbohydrate load triggers an insulin surge that drives phosphate, potassium, and magnesium into cells, causing arrhythmias and respiratory failure.
Thiamine deficiency worsens the risk, so it is given before or with the first feeding.
Full-rate starts, delayed replacement, and infrequent labs all miss the early drop in electrolytes.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with long-term benzodiazepine use is found drowsy after taking an unknown number of tablets, including a tricyclic antidepressant. Breathing is shallow. What should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Observation alone, as the client is still breathing
options.B: Immediate flumazenil to restore full alertness
options.C: Naloxone as the first treatment and the sole therapy at this time at this time
options.D: Airway and ventilation support; flumazenil may trigger seizures in this client

questions.correct_text: Airway and ventilation support; flumazenil may trigger seizures in this client
explanation: Flumazenil can cause seizures in clients with long-term benzodiazepine use or tricyclic ingestion.
Supporting breathing is the safest first step.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A small-bore feeding tube is clogged. Which action should the nurse try first?

options.A: Flush with warm water using gentle push and pull motions
options.B: Insert a thin wire stylet into the tube to break up the clog
options.C: Instill cola and clamp the tube for 30 minutes before flushing
options.D: Force 60 mL of water through the tube with one firm, steady push

questions.correct_text: Flush with warm water using gentle push and pull motions
explanation: Warm water and gentle pressure are safest.
Wires can puncture the tube or the bowel, and force can burst the tube.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Eight hours after a thyroidectomy, a client reports tingling around the mouth. When the nurse inflates a BP cuff on the arm, the hand curls into a spasm. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Treat the tingling as anxiety and coach slow breathing with a paper bag
options.B: Expect normal postoperative numbness and recheck the client in the morning right now
options.C: Suspect low calcium and keep airway equipment and IV calcium gluconate ready
options.D: Give a potassium supplement and recheck the potassium level later tonight

questions.correct_text: Suspect low calcium and keep airway equipment and IV calcium gluconate ready
explanation: Injury or removal of the parathyroid glands lowers calcium, which causes tingling and spasm (Trousseau sign).
Severe hypocalcemia can cause laryngospasm and seizures.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A hiker has a venomous snake bite on the lower leg. Which action is correct?

options.A: Keep the limb still near heart level, remove rings, and go to emergency care
options.B: Apply a tight tourniquet above the bite to stop the venom from spreading
options.C: Cut across the bite and suck out the venom with the mouth right away
options.D: Apply ice directly on the bite to slow the spread of the venom in the leg for the moment

questions.correct_text: Keep the limb still near heart level, remove rings, and go to emergency care
explanation: Immobility slows spread of venom, and swelling is expected so rings are removed.
Cutting, sucking, ice, and tourniquets cause tissue damage.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client receiving continuous tube feeding has the feeding held for a procedure for 4 hours. Intermediate-acting insulin is due. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Give the full dose as ordered
options.B: Skip the dose and the glucose checks
options.C: Give the full dose with orange juice right now
options.D: Check the glucose before giving any insulin

questions.correct_text: Check the glucose before giving any insulin
explanation: Insulin without the usual calories can cause hypoglycemia.
The glucose is monitored, and the dose is reviewed.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Tube feeding held while insulin is due

questions.question: An infant weighed 11.2 kg at a well visit and weighs 10.4 kg after 3 days of vomiting and diarrhea. What is the estimated fluid loss and degree of dehydration?

options.A: About 80 mL, or about 0.7%
options.B: About 800 mL, or about 7%
options.C: About 800 mL, or about 15%
options.D: About 1,100 mL, or about 10%

questions.correct_text: About 800 mL, or about 7%
explanation: Weight loss is 0.8 kg, and 1 kg of acute weight loss equals about 1 liter of fluid.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A nurse irrigates a deep wound with a syringe. Which technique is correct?

options.A: Press the syringe tip firmly into the wound bed to give the stream more force
options.B: Irrigate from the dirtiest area toward the cleanest area, holding the tip close
options.C: Irrigate from the cleanest area toward the dirtiest, keeping the tip clear of the wound
options.D: Use the same gloves for irrigation and the dressing without hand hygiene in between for now

questions.correct_text: Irrigate from the cleanest area toward the dirtiest, keeping the tip clear of the wound
explanation: Flow from clean to dirty keeps contamination from spreading to cleaner tissue.
The tip does not touch the wound, which keeps the irrigant sterile.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with diabetes has a painless ulcer over the ball of the foot with a thick callus rim and normal pulses. What is the priority intervention?

options.A: Soak the foot in hot water for comfort
options.B: Remove the callus at home with a razor
options.C: Walk barefoot to improve circulation
options.D: Offload the pressure with special footwear and inspect the foot each day

questions.correct_text: Offload the pressure with special footwear and inspect the foot each day
explanation: Loss of sensation lets pressure injure the foot without pain.
Pressure relief allows healing.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A tube feeding starts at 20 mL/hr and increases by 10 mL/hr every 4 hours until the goal of 60 mL/hr is reached. How many hours after the start will the goal rate begin?

options.A: 20 hours
options.B: 24 hours
options.C: 16 hours
options.D: 12 hours

questions.correct_text: 16 hours
explanation: The rate goes 20, 30 (4 hours), 40 (8 hours), 50 (12 hours), and 60 (16 hours).
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client 1 day after hip surgery has an order for knee-high antiembolism stockings. The feet are cool, pedal pulses are barely palpable, capillary refill is 5 seconds, and the client has a history of leg pain when walking and an ankle-brachial index of 0.4. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Withhold the stockings and check the circulation in the feet
options.B: Apply a sequential compression device in place of the stockings
options.C: Apply the stockings and check the toes every 8 hours
options.D: Apply the stockings with a larger size for comfort

questions.correct_text: Withhold the stockings and check the circulation in the feet
explanation: Severe peripheral arterial disease limits leg blood flow, and compression can cause ischemia or tissue death.
Compression devices also reduce arterial flow in this setting.
A different size or more frequent checks do not remove the risk.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with suspected meningitis has a lumbar puncture. Which cerebrospinal fluid result is most consistent with a bacterial cause?

options.A: Clear fluid, normal protein, normal glucose, and a few cells at this time
options.B: Clear fluid, mild increase in lymphocytes, normal glucose
options.C: Cloudy fluid, high white cell count, high protein, and low glucose
options.D: Bloody fluid that clears in later tubes

questions.correct_text: Cloudy fluid, high white cell count, high protein, and low glucose
explanation: Bacteria and the response of the body to them make the fluid cloudy and use up the glucose.
Viral causes usually give clear fluid with normal glucose.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: One 300 mL unit of red cells is ordered over 3 hours. Policy requires the first 15 minutes at 2 mL/min. After the first 15 minutes, what pump rate in mL/hr infuses the rest in the remaining time? (Round to the nearest whole number.)

options.A: 100 mL/hr
options.B: 90 mL/hr
options.C: 108 mL/hr
options.D: 98 mL/hr

questions.correct_text: 98 mL/hr
explanation: First 15 minutes: 2 x 15 = 30 mL, leaving 270 mL.
Remaining time: 180 - 15 = 165 minutes (2.75 hours); 270 / 2.75 = 98 mL/hr.
100 ignores the first 15 minutes; 90 uses the full 3 hours.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: On day 6 after abdominal surgery, a client coughs and reports that something gave way. Pink watery fluid soaks through the dressing, and the incision looks open. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Push any exposed tissue back into the abdomen
options.B: Apply a tight abdominal binder to close the wound
options.C: Cover the wound with a sterile saline-moistened dressing and keep the client lying low with the knees bent
options.D: Reinforce the dressing and reassess in the morning today as planned

questions.correct_text: Cover the wound with a sterile saline-moistened dressing and keep the client lying low with the knees bent
explanation: A sudden opening of the incision with fluid drainage suggests the layers have separated.
Moist sterile coverage and rest protect the tissue until the surgeon sees the client.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A central line hub cracks and detaches during a tubing change. The client suddenly becomes dyspneic and anxious, with SpO2 85%, chest pain, and HR 130. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Clamp the catheter and place the client on the left side in Trendelenburg
options.B: Place the client in high Fowler's position and apply oxygen by mask
options.C: Apply a nonrebreather mask and place the client flat in the supine position
options.D: Attach a syringe to the catheter hub and try to aspirate the air out

questions.correct_text: Clamp the catheter and place the client on the left side in Trendelenburg
explanation: The cues point to air entering through the open catheter; closing the catheter stops more air from entering.
Left side-lying with the head down traps air in the right atrium away from the pulmonary outflow.
Oxygen follows right after; high Fowler's lets air travel to the lungs, and aspiration is a provider skill.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Air entry through a central line

questions.question: A client with a known ragweed allergy develops hives and an itchy mouth after drinking chamomile tea. What does the nurse understand about this reaction?

options.A: The tea is a safe herbal product that cannot cause an allergic reaction for the moment
options.B: The reaction is a side effect of the tea's caffeine content
options.C: The reaction means the client is allergic to every herbal product
options.D: Chamomile can cross-react with ragweed pollen, so the client should avoid it

questions.correct_text: Chamomile can cross-react with ragweed pollen, so the client should avoid it
explanation: Plants in the same family can share proteins that trigger allergy.
The client avoids chamomile and similar herbs, and the reaction is treated as an allergy.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A nurse leaves the room of a client on contact and droplet precautions. Place the steps in order: 1 Remove the gown. 2 Remove the gloves. 3 Perform hand hygiene. 4 Remove the mask. 5 Remove the goggles. Which order is correct?
explanation: Gloves are the most contaminated and come off first, then eye protection, then the gown.
The mask is removed last among the items, and hand hygiene follows removal of all equipment.
Removing the mask or gown first spreads contamination to the face and hands.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: An angry visitor shouts at the nurse at the bedside of a client. Which nurse action is best?

options.A: Stay calm, keep a safe distance and an open path to the exit, speak in a low voice, and call security if the behavior escalates
options.B: Argue the points the visitor raises until the visitor calms down for now
options.C: Block the doorway so the visitor cannot leave the room
options.D: Stand close to the visitor and match the voice level to be heard

questions.correct_text: Stay calm, keep a safe distance and an open path to the exit, speak in a low voice, and call security if the behavior escalates
explanation: A calm approach with space and an exit protects the nurse and avoids escalation.
Security is called early if the situation does not settle.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Safe response to an agitated visitor

questions.question: A client after a stroke has right homonymous hemianopsia and misses the food on the right side of the tray. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Feed the client each meal so the client does not miss food on the right side
options.B: Place the tray on the right side so that the client gets practice looking there
options.C: Remove the tray and offer a snack later when the client is less frustrated
options.D: Place items in the client's intact left field and teach head turning to scan

questions.correct_text: Place items in the client's intact left field and teach head turning to scan
explanation: The client cannot see the right half of each visual field, so items are placed where they can be seen.
Scanning teaches the client to compensate and keeps independence.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client 2 weeks after a viral illness has weakness that began in the feet and is moving up the legs. Reflexes are absent. What is the nurse's priority?

options.A: Monitor breathing, including vital capacity; the weakness can reach the respiratory muscles
options.B: Reassure the client and recheck in 24 hours
options.C: Encourage vigorous exercise to rebuild strength right now
options.D: Give a sedative for the discomfort

questions.correct_text: Monitor breathing, including vital capacity; the weakness can reach the respiratory muscles
explanation: Ascending paralysis with absent reflexes suggests Guillain-Barre syndrome.
Respiratory failure is the most serious risk.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Ascending weakness after a viral illness

questions.question: Blood is drawn from the arm above an infusing IV of 5% dextrose in water. Results: glucose 640 mg/dL, sodium 128 mEq/L, potassium 2.4 mEq/L, creatinine normal. The client's glucose was 110 this morning and the client is asymptomatic. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Treat the hyperglycemia now
options.B: Repeat the draw from the opposite arm
options.C: Send a urine glucose
options.D: Replace the potassium immediately at this time

questions.correct_text: Repeat the draw from the opposite arm
explanation: IV fluid in the sample dilutes electrolytes and raises glucose, which accounts for the pattern.
A repeat from the other arm confirms before treatment.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Lab results from a contaminated sample

questions.question: A nurse prepares to give enoxaparin from a prefilled syringe that contains a small air bubble. Which action is correct?

options.A: Expel the air bubble from the syringe before injecting into the abdomen as planned
options.B: Massage the injection site after giving the drug to help it spread
options.C: Leave the air bubble in place and inject into the abdomen without rubbing
options.D: Aspirate for blood return before injecting the drug into the abdomen

questions.correct_text: Leave the air bubble in place and inject into the abdomen without rubbing
explanation: The air bubble clears the drug from the needle and prevents leaking along the track, and expelling it wastes drug.
Aspiration and rubbing increase bruising at the site.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with type 2 diabetes and an eGFR of 38 mL/min takes metformin and is scheduled for an IV contrast CT. What should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Giving the metformin as usual with the morning meal and a glass of water
options.B: Giving an extra dose of metformin before the scan to protect the kidneys right now
options.C: Stopping the insulin and withholding oral fluids until after the scan
options.D: Holding the metformin per protocol and checking kidney function afterward

questions.correct_text: Holding the metformin per protocol and checking kidney function afterward
explanation: Contrast can injure the kidneys, and metformin accumulates when kidney function falls, which raises the risk of lactic acidosis.
The drug is held and restarted after kidney function is confirmed.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: With a client at 45 degrees, the nurse sees the top of the jugular vein pulsation 6 cm above the sternal angle. How should the nurse interpret this?

options.A: Elevated central venous pressure, as seen in volume overload or right heart failure
options.B: Low central venous pressure from dehydration
options.C: A normal finding for a client sitting at 45 degrees
options.D: A sign limited to aortic valve disease

questions.correct_text: Elevated central venous pressure, as seen in volume overload or right heart failure
explanation: The normal level is less than about 3 cm above the sternal angle.
A higher level suggests that blood is backing up toward the right heart.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: An older adult is found in a hot apartment with a temperature of 41.2 C, hot dry skin, confusion, and HR 128. What is the priority intervention?

options.A: Give acetaminophen by mouth and recheck the temperature in an hour for the moment
options.B: Wrap the client in warm blankets and offer sips of warm tea
options.C: Give salt tablets with a large glass of fluid to replace losses
options.D: Begin rapid cooling with cold packs at the neck, armpits, and groin

questions.correct_text: Begin rapid cooling with cold packs at the neck, armpits, and groin
explanation: Heat stroke damages organs rapidly, so core temperature must fall quickly.
Antipyretics do not work because the problem is failed heat loss, not a reset set point.
A confused client should not be given oral intake.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Six hours after cardiac surgery, a client has BP 82/60 and falling, HR 126, distended neck veins, muffled heart sounds, and chest tube drainage that has suddenly stopped. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Prepare for pericardial drainage or return to surgery while calling for urgent help
options.B: Strip the chest tube toward the drainage unit and milk the clots out of it
options.C: Lay the client flat, give a prescribed analgesic, and recheck in 30 minutes
options.D: Give a large fluid bolus and recheck the blood pressure and heart rate in 1 hour as planned

questions.correct_text: Prepare for pericardial drainage or return to surgery while calling for urgent help
explanation: Falling BP, distended neck veins, and muffled heart sounds point to fluid or blood compressing the heart.
Drainage stopping suddenly suggests clotted tubes with blood collecting around the heart.
Stripping tubing and waiting do not relieve the compression.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A parent plans to add honey to the cereal of a 7-month-old to make it more appealing. What should the nurse advise?

options.A: Honey can be used in small amounts if the infant tolerates it well at this time
options.B: Honey is safe when it is mixed with formula
options.C: Honey is safe if it is pasteurized and mixed with warm cereal
options.D: Avoid honey until after 12 months of age; it carries a risk of infant botulism

questions.correct_text: Avoid honey until after 12 months of age; it carries a risk of infant botulism
explanation: Honey can contain spores that grow in an infant's immature gut.
Heating or mixing does not remove the risk.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: The laboratory reports a potassium of 6.6 mEq/L on a sample marked "hemolyzed." The client has normal kidney function, a normal ECG, no symptoms, and takes no medication that raises potassium. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Give sodium polystyrene sulfonate by mouth
options.B: Request a repeat draw before any treatment
options.C: Place the client on seizure precautions
options.D: Give regular insulin with dextrose now

questions.correct_text: Request a repeat draw before any treatment
explanation: Broken red cells release potassium into the sample, causing a falsely high value.
A normal ECG, no risk factors, and no symptoms support an artifact.
Treating a false value risks dangerous hypokalemia.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A nurse sets up a sterile field, and a spill of saline soaks through the sterile drape onto the table beneath. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Blot the wet area with a sterile gauze and continue
options.B: Cover the wet area with a second sterile drape
options.C: Consider the field contaminated and set up a new one
options.D: Continue using the field if the supplies are on the dry area

questions.correct_text: Consider the field contaminated and set up a new one
explanation: Moisture carries organisms through the drape by wicking, so a wet field is no longer sterile.
The field and the supplies on it are replaced.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client scheduled for surgery tomorrow takes empagliflozin daily. What should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: A hold of the drug for several days before surgery, to lower the risk of ketoacidosis
options.B: Continuing the drug without change
options.C: Giving a double dose on the morning of surgery
options.D: Stopping the drug after the surgery

questions.correct_text: A hold of the drug for several days before surgery, to lower the risk of ketoacidosis
explanation: This drug class can cause ketoacidosis during fasting and surgical stress.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Order: heparin bolus 80 units/kg IV. The client weighs 70 kg. The vial contains 5,000 units/mL. How many mL should the nurse draw up? (Round to the nearest tenth.)

options.A: 5.6 mL
options.B: 0.9 mL
options.C: 1.1 mL

questions.correct_text: 1.1 mL
explanation: Dose: 80 x 70 = 5,600 units.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A worker arrives after contact with a high-voltage line. The skin shows just small entrance and exit burns, and the worker feels fine. What should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Discharge after a dressing is applied to the small burns at this time
options.B: A tetanus booster as the sole treatment
options.C: Oral fluids and observation for one hour
options.D: Continuous cardiac monitoring and IV fluids; deep tissue damage can be hidden

questions.correct_text: Continuous cardiac monitoring and IV fluids; deep tissue damage can be hidden
explanation: The current travels through the body, which can cause arrhythmias and muscle breakdown.
Small skin burns can hide large internal injury.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A trauma victim arrives after a fall from a height. Which step is first in the primary survey?

options.A: Open and protect the airway while keeping the cervical spine in line
options.B: Examine the abdomen for tenderness
options.C: Check the blood pressure and heart rate
options.D: Remove the clothing to look for injuries

questions.correct_text: Open and protect the airway while keeping the cervical spine in line
explanation: The order is airway with spine protection, breathing, circulation, disability, and exposure.
An airway problem kills fastest.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Two hours after the first dose of lisinopril, a client has swelling of the lips and tongue and a hoarse voice. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Apply ice to the lips and recheck in an hour
options.B: Stop further doses, maintain the airway, and prepare emergency airway equipment
options.C: Give the next dose on schedule and watch the swelling for the moment
options.D: Give an antacid and elevate the head of the bed

questions.correct_text: Stop further doses, maintain the airway, and prepare emergency airway equipment
explanation: Angioedema from an ACE inhibitor can block the airway.
The drug is stopped, and the airway is the priority.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Lip swelling after a first ACE inhibitor dose

questions.question: A 70-year-old male weighs 75 kg and has a serum creatinine of 1.4 mg/dL. Using the Cockcroft-Gault formula [(140 - age) x weight / (72 x creatinine)], what is the estimated creatinine clearance?

options.A: 52 mL/min
options.B: 104 mL/min
options.C: 73 mL/min
options.D: 44 mL/min

questions.correct_text: 52 mL/min
explanation: 73 results from using a creatinine of 1.0.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with a sodium of 112 mEq/L and confusion is receiving 3% sodium chloride. At 12 hours the sodium is 127 mEq/L, and the client is alert and oriented. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Continue the infusion until the sodium reaches 135 mEq/L
options.B: Slow the infusion by half and recheck the sodium in 12 hours for now
options.C: Stop the infusion and monitor neurologic status and sodium levels
options.D: Change to 0.9% sodium chloride at the same rate

questions.correct_text: Stop the infusion and monitor neurologic status and sodium levels
explanation: A 15 mEq/L rise in 12 hours exceeds the usual safe limit of about 8 to 10 mEq/L in 24 hours and raises the risk of osmotic demyelination.
Symptoms have resolved, so more hypertonic saline is not needed.
Halving the rate or switching fluids at the same rate still allows the sodium to climb too fast.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client receiving a heparin infusion (target aPTT 60 to 80 seconds) has an aPTT of 112 seconds and a new nosebleed. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Continue the infusion and repeat the aPTT in 24 hours
options.B: Hold the infusion per protocol and assess for bleeding
options.C: Give vitamin K to reverse the heparin
options.D: Increase the infusion rate to maintain therapeutic effect

questions.correct_text: Hold the infusion per protocol and assess for bleeding
explanation: An aPTT well above target with active bleeding calls for stopping the drug and assessing for blood loss.
Protamine reverses heparin, and vitamin K does not.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Heparin infusion with a high aPTT

questions.question: A client has a respiratory rate of 28/min and a tidal volume of 250 mL. What is the minute ventilation, and what does it suggest?

options.A: 7 L/min, a normal total with rapid, shallow breaths that move little air to the gas-exchange areas
options.B: 0.9 L/min, a sign of slow breathing
options.C: 7 L/min, a sign of deep breathing
options.D: 280 L/min, a dangerous level

questions.correct_text: 7 L/min, a normal total with rapid, shallow breaths that move little air to the gas-exchange areas
explanation: Shallow breaths ventilate dead space, so the client may still have poor gas exchange.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has sodium 140 mEq/L, glucose 90 mg/dL, and BUN 14 mg/dL. Using osmolality = 2 x sodium + glucose/18 + BUN/2.8, what is the calculated osmolality?

options.A: About 245 mOsm/kg
options.B: About 290 mOsm/kg
options.C: About 330 mOsm/kg
options.D: About 160 mOsm/kg

questions.correct_text: About 290 mOsm/kg
explanation: The total is 290 mOsm/kg, within the normal range.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with a nasogastric tube to low suction for 3 days has an ABG of pH 7.52, PaCO2 46, and HCO3 36. Which laboratory abnormality is most likely?

options.A: High chloride
options.B: High phosphate
options.C: High calcium
options.D: Low potassium

questions.correct_text: Low potassium
explanation: Loss of gastric acid causes metabolic alkalosis with low chloride.
Kidneys then excrete potassium to hold on to hydrogen ions, which lowers potassium.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client reports an "allergy to codeine" and explains, "It makes me vomit." What should the nurse do?

options.A: Question the client about the reaction and record nausea as a side effect, not a true allergy
options.B: Ignore the statement, as nausea is not an allergic reaction to a drug
options.C: Give codeine with an antiemetic to prevent the nausea and vomiting it causes at this time for now
options.D: List codeine as a severe allergy and notify the pharmacy of the reaction

questions.correct_text: Question the client about the reaction and record nausea as a side effect, not a true allergy
explanation: A true allergy involves immune signs such as hives, swelling, wheezing, or anaphylaxis.
Accurate documentation avoids withholding useful drugs and keeps true allergies visible.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client eats black licorice daily and has a potassium of 3.1 mEq/L and BP 160/98. What is the likely link?

options.A: Licorice raises potassium
options.B: Licorice lowers blood pressure
options.C: Licorice can cause the body to retain sodium and lose potassium
options.D: Licorice has no effect on the body

questions.correct_text: Licorice can cause the body to retain sodium and lose potassium
explanation: Real licorice has a compound that acts like a hormone that retains salt and water.
This raises blood pressure and lowers potassium.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client receiving parenteral nutrition has a glucose of 310 mg/dL. The nurse is considering stopping the infusion. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Increase the infusion rate to meet the calorie goal at this time
options.B: Continue the infusion at the ordered rate and monitor the glucose closely
options.C: Replace the bag with 0.9% sodium chloride
options.D: Stop the infusion at once until the glucose falls

questions.correct_text: Continue the infusion at the ordered rate and monitor the glucose closely
explanation: Stopping the high-dextrose infusion suddenly can cause rebound low glucose.
Insulin treats the high value while the feeding continues.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Which nursing diagnosis is written correctly?

options.A: Pressure ulcer related to bed rest
options.B: Risk for infection as evidenced by an incision that is red and draining
options.C: Impaired skin integrity related to prolonged immobility, as evidenced by a 3-cm stage 2 sacral pressure injury
options.D: Fear related to a diagnosis of cancer

questions.correct_text: Impaired skin integrity related to prolonged immobility, as evidenced by a 3-cm stage 2 sacral pressure injury
explanation: A nursing diagnosis has a problem, a related cause, and evidence, and it is not a medical diagnosis.
A risk diagnosis has no evidence of a current problem.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: While scanning IV ampicillin for a client, the computer displays a penicillin allergy alert. The client reports a past rash. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Hold the dose and gather the details of the reported reaction
options.B: Give a PRN antihistamine first, then give the antibiotic as scheduled on the MAR
