questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Nitroglycerin and an erectile dysfunction drug

questions.question: A client with heart failure has crackles, jugular vein distention, and a 3 kg weight gain in 2 days. The provider writes four orders. Which order should the nurse question?

options.A: Daily weights each morning before breakfast on the same scale
options.B: Restrict sodium intake to 2 grams daily and teach label reading
options.C: Furosemide 40 mg IV once now with monitoring of urine output
options.D: 0.9% sodium chloride 1,000 mL IV bolus over 30 minutes

questions.correct_text: 0.9% sodium chloride 1,000 mL IV bolus over 30 minutes
explanation: The client is volume overloaded, and a large bolus could cause pulmonary edema.
Diuresis, daily weights, and sodium restriction are expected treatments.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client in the recovery room has an Aldrete score of 2 for activity, 2 for respiration, 2 for circulation, 1 for consciousness, and 1 for color. What is the total score, and what does it mean?

options.A: 8; the client is not yet ready for discharge from the unit (a score of 9 or more is expected)
options.B: 10; the client is fully recovered
options.C: 8; the client is ready for discharge from the unit
options.D: 6; the client needs immediate resuscitation

questions.correct_text: 8; the client is not yet ready for discharge from the unit (a score of 9 or more is expected)
explanation: The scores add to 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 8.
A score of 9 or more is usually required for discharge from the unit.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client who stopped drinking alcohol 3 days ago reports vivid dreams and frequent waking. What should the nurse explain?

options.A: The dreams show a new mental illness
options.B: Alcohol suppresses dream (REM) sleep, and rebound after stopping causes vivid dreams that usually settle
options.C: Sleep is not affected by alcohol
options.D: The dreams are caused by the hospital food

questions.correct_text: Alcohol suppresses dream (REM) sleep, and rebound after stopping causes vivid dreams that usually settle
explanation: REM sleep is reduced by alcohol and returns with an increase when it is stopped.
Sleep hygiene helps.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has an eGFR of 25 mL/min and a potassium of 5.4 mEq/L. Which order should the nurse question?

options.A: Teaching on a low-potassium diet
options.B: A repeat potassium level in the morning
options.C: Furosemide 40 mg IV once to promote potassium loss at this time today for the moment
options.D: Spironolactone 50 mg daily together with potassium chloride 20 mEq daily

questions.correct_text: Spironolactone 50 mg daily together with potassium chloride 20 mEq daily
explanation: Spironolactone holds potassium in the body, and added potassium raises it more in failing kidneys.
A loop diuretic, a repeat level, and diet teaching are appropriate.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A tall, thin client has sudden pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea. On the right side, the nurse finds a hyperresonant percussion note, absent breath sounds, and decreased fremitus. What do these findings suggest?

options.A: Pneumonia with consolidation
options.B: A pneumothorax
options.C: Pulmonary edema
options.D: A pleural effusion

questions.correct_text: A pneumothorax
explanation: Air in the pleural space gives a hyperresonant sound and no breath sounds.
Fluid and consolidation give dullness.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with asthma has a personal best peak flow of 400 L/min. Today the reading is 220 L/min, and the client has a cough. Which interpretation and action are correct?

options.A: Yellow zone at 55% of personal best; use the quick-relief inhaler and follow the plan
options.B: Red zone at 55% of personal best; call emergency services for transport right away
options.C: Yellow zone at 45% of personal best; increase the daily controller medication dose
options.D: Green zone at 55% of personal best; continue daily controller medication and normal activity

questions.correct_text: Yellow zone at 55% of personal best; use the quick-relief inhaler and follow the plan
explanation: 220 / 400 = 55%, which falls in the yellow zone (50 to 80%).
Yellow zone means worsening control and needs a quick-relief inhaler and reassessment, with escalation if there is no improvement.
Red is below 50% and needs emergency treatment.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client receives propofol at 12 mL/hr for 24 hours. Propofol provides 1.1 kcal/mL. How many kilocalories does the client receive from the drug in a day?

options.A: About 1,100 kcal
options.B: About 288 kcal
options.C: About 317 kcal
options.D: About 13 kcal

questions.correct_text: About 317 kcal
explanation: 12 x 24 = 288 mL per day.
288 x 1.1 = about 317 kcal, which counts toward the daily nutrition.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client on day 2 after a stroke is helped to dangle at the bedside. After 3 minutes, BP falls from 128/76 to 84/50, and the client reports dizziness and looks pale. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Give a glass of water and keep the client sitting upright
options.B: Return the client to a lying position and hold activity until blood pressure is stable
options.C: Continue dangling for 5 more minutes so the client can adapt for the moment as planned
options.D: Stand the client at the bedside to speed the adaptation

questions.correct_text: Return the client to a lying position and hold activity until blood pressure is stable
explanation: A large drop in pressure with symptoms signals that the client cannot tolerate the upright position yet.
Lying flat restores brain blood flow, and the activity is advanced in small steps later.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client 3 weeks after a partial gastrectomy becomes shaky, sweaty, and weak 2 hours after meals. The glucose is 55 mg/dL during an episode. What should the nurse teach?

options.A: Eat small meals with protein and complex carbohydrates and limit concentrated sweets
options.B: Drink fluids with meals to help the food pass
options.C: Lie down right after meals and avoid snacks between meals as planned
options.D: Eat large meals with plenty of juice to raise the glucose

questions.correct_text: Eat small meals with protein and complex carbohydrates and limit concentrated sweets
explanation: Fast emptying of sugar into the bowel causes a surge of insulin and a later low glucose.
Small meals with protein and complex carbohydrate slow the emptying.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: During general anesthesia with succinylcholine and sevoflurane, a client's end-tidal CO2 rises sharply, the jaw is rigid, temperature is 39.8 C, and HR is 142. What should the nurse anticipate first?

options.A: Giving more succinylcholine to relax the rigid muscles and lower heat
options.B: Stopping the triggering anesthetic agents and preparing IV dantrolene
options.C: Giving acetaminophen and applying a cooling blanket as the first measures
options.D: Restricting fluids and monitoring the temperature every 15 minutes

questions.correct_text: Stopping the triggering anesthetic agents and preparing IV dantrolene
explanation: This pattern is typical of a hypermetabolic crisis triggered by anesthetic agents.
Removing the triggers and giving dantrolene stops the rise in muscle metabolism.
Cooling alone does not treat the cause, and more succinylcholine worsens it.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with capacity wants to leave against medical advice before treatment is complete. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Explain the risks, document the client's decision, and have the client sign the AMA form
options.B: Refuse to remove the IV catheter until the provider has agreed to the discharge right now
options.C: Tell the client that insurance will not pay for the stay after leaving early
options.D: Lock the door to stop the client from leaving until the provider comes to talk

questions.correct_text: Explain the risks, document the client's decision, and have the client sign the AMA form
explanation: A client with capacity has the right to leave.
The nurse makes sure the risks are understood, informs the provider, and documents the process.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: An 86-year-old client whose usual temperature is 36.0 C now has a temperature of 37.5 C and new confusion. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Give acetaminophen and observe the temperature and the confusion overnight
options.B: Recheck the temperature in 24 hours and continue to watch the confusion
options.C: Document a normal temperature, as the reading is below the 38 C fever mark
options.D: Treat it as a possible infection; the rise from baseline is significant

questions.correct_text: Treat it as a possible infection; the rise from baseline is significant
explanation: Older adults have lower baselines, and a rise of about 1.1 C above baseline can signal infection.
New confusion makes infection more likely, and waiting delays treatment.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has negative pressure wound therapy on a sacral wound. The seal-loss alarm sounds, and the nurse cannot restore the seal after checking the tubing and dressing edges. The therapy has been off for 3 hours. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Remove the foam dressing and apply a moist saline gauze dressing
options.B: Leave the foam in place until the next scheduled dressing change
options.C: Clamp the tubing and leave the foam in place overnight
options.D: Cover the foam with an occlusive film and restart at a lower pressure

questions.correct_text: Remove the foam dressing and apply a moist saline gauze dressing
explanation: Foam left in a wound without suction for longer than about 2 hours can trap exudate and bacteria and may become embedded.
A moist saline dressing protects the wound until therapy can be restored.
Restarting or waiting leaves the foam in a wound that is no longer draining.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has sudden left-sided weakness and slurred speech. A family member says, "Give the aspirin from the cabinet." What should the nurse do?

options.A: Give a double dose to help it work faster
options.B: Give the aspirin and then call the provider
options.C: Give the aspirin right away to thin the blood right now today for the moment
options.D: Hold the aspirin until imaging rules out bleeding in the brain

questions.correct_text: Hold the aspirin until imaging rules out bleeding in the brain
explanation: A stroke can be caused by bleeding, and aspirin could make it worse.
The type of stroke must be known before treatment is chosen.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Aspirin for a stroke before imaging

questions.question: A client taking ibuprofen for 2 weeks reports black stools. BP is 104/66 (usually 134/82), HR is 112, hemoglobin is 8.1 g/dL (12.6 yesterday), BUN is 52 mg/dL, and creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Encourage oral fluids to correct the elevated BUN level before further tests
options.B: Insert a second large-bore IV and prepare for transfusion needs
options.C: Send a stool specimen for occult blood testing and a repeat hemoglobin
options.D: Hold the next ibuprofen dose and document the stool color and amount

questions.correct_text: Insert a second large-bore IV and prepare for transfusion needs
explanation: Falling hemoglobin, tachycardia, and a drop in BP show active blood loss; circulation support comes first.
BUN rises with a normal creatinine because digested blood adds protein load, so this is not simple dehydration.
Stool testing adds nothing now, and holding ibuprofen, while needed, does not treat the unstable circulation.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Thirty hours after a femur fracture, a client develops sudden dyspnea, confusion, SpO2 85%, and small red-purple spots on the chest and armpits. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Apply high-flow oxygen and raise the head of the bed
options.B: Place a sequential compression device on the injured leg
options.C: Encourage deep breathing and recheck in 1 hour
options.D: Apply a heating pad to the injured leg

questions.correct_text: Apply high-flow oxygen and raise the head of the bed
explanation: Dyspnea, confusion, and petechiae after a long-bone fracture suggest fat droplets in the lungs and brain.
Oxygen and rapid help are needed, and compression devices or heat do not help.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A dying client has noisy, wet respirations. The daughter is crying and says, "He's drowning." Which nurse action is best?

options.A: Perform deep suctioning right away and ask the provider to order a chest x-ray for now
options.B: Turn the client to the side, give the anticholinergic, and explain the sound to her
options.C: Increase the IV fluid rate and ask the provider about adding a mucolytic
options.D: Raise the head of the bed to 90 degrees and apply a high-flow oxygen mask

questions.correct_text: Turn the client to the side, give the anticholinergic, and explain the sound to her
explanation: Terminal secretions come from a weakened swallow and cough, and the client is usually not aware of them.
Positioning, drying medication, and family explanation address comfort and fear.
Deep suction irritates the airway, and extra fluid worsens secretions.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A child weighs 33 lb. The order is 0.1 mg/kg IV. The vial contains 2 mg/mL. How many mL should the nurse give?

options.B: 3.3 mL

explanation: 1.5 mg / 2 mg per mL = 0.75 mL.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Unit conversion for a pediatric dose

questions.question: Order: regular insulin infusion at 0.1 unit/kg/hr. The client weighs 185 lb. The bag contains 100 units in 100 mL. What rate in mL/hr should the nurse set? (Round to the nearest tenth.)

options.A: 84.1 mL/hr
options.B: 8.4 mL/hr
options.C: 18.5 mL/hr
options.D: 0.8 mL/hr

questions.correct_text: 8.4 mL/hr
explanation: 0.1 x 84.1 = 8.4 units/hr; at 1 unit/mL the rate is 8.4 mL/hr.
18.5 results from using pounds; the other values are decimal errors.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has an area of burned skin that is white and leathery with no pain when touched. How is this burn classified?

options.A: Full-thickness
options.B: Superficial partial-thickness
options.C: Superficial
options.D: Deep partial-thickness

questions.correct_text: Full-thickness
explanation: A full-thickness burn destroys the nerve endings, so it is painless and leathery or waxy.
Partial-thickness burns are painful with blisters.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A parenteral nutrition order includes 1,000 mL of 25% dextrose (3.4 kcal/g) and 250 mL of 20% lipid emulsion (2 kcal/mL). How many kilocalories does the client receive in this order?

options.A: 850 kcal
options.B: 2,100 kcal
options.C: 1,700 kcal
options.D: 1,350 kcal

questions.correct_text: 1,350 kcal
explanation: Dextrose: 250 g x 3.4 = 850 kcal.
Lipid: 250 mL x 2 = 500 kcal; total 1,350 kcal.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with a head injury has pupils that were equal and reactive an hour ago. Now the right pupil is 6 mm and fixed, and the left is 3 mm and reactive. The client is more drowsy. What does this suggest?

options.A: Eye strain from the bright lighting in the intensive care unit overnight
options.B: Compression of the oculomotor nerve from rising intracranial pressure
options.C: An effect of eye drops given earlier during the emergency department visit
options.D: A normal variation in pupil size that does not need follow-up care

questions.correct_text: Compression of the oculomotor nerve from rising intracranial pressure
explanation: A new fixed, dilated pupil with decreasing alertness suggests pressure on the third cranial nerve from brain swelling or bleeding.
The change from a known baseline makes a normal variation unlikely.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Insulin lispro 8 units is due at 0730 "with breakfast," and the glucose is 232 mg/dL. The tray will be delayed 45 minutes. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Hold the insulin until the tray is at the bedside, then give it
options.B: Give the insulin on time and recheck the glucose after the meal
options.C: Give the insulin now and offer juice in 30 minutes if needed
options.D: Give half the dose now and the other half when the meal arrives

questions.correct_text: Hold the insulin until the tray is at the bedside, then give it
explanation: Rapid-acting insulin begins working in 10 to 20 minutes and can cause hypoglycemia without food.
The dose is given when the meal is ready to be eaten.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Rapid-acting insulin and a delayed meal

questions.question: A child weighs 44 lb. The order is amoxicillin 40 mg/kg/day divided every 8 hours. The suspension is 250 mg/5 mL. How many mL should the nurse give per dose? (Round to the nearest tenth.)

options.A: 16 mL
options.B: 5.3 mL
options.C: 8 mL
options.D: 2.7 mL

questions.correct_text: 5.3 mL
explanation: 44 lb / 2.2 = 20 kg; 20 x 40 = 800 mg per day.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Divided daily dose for a child

questions.question: A client with a catheter in place for 3 weeks has fever and cloudy urine. A urine culture is ordered. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Replace the catheter, then collect the specimen from the new catheter
options.B: Collect the specimen from the old drainage bag
options.C: Collect the specimen after emptying the bag into a container at this time
options.D: Disconnect the tubing and collect urine from the open end

questions.correct_text: Replace the catheter, then collect the specimen from the new catheter
explanation: Bacteria grow in a film on the old catheter, so a specimen from it can misrepresent the bladder.
A new catheter gives a more accurate sample.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Urine specimen from a long-term catheter

questions.question: A client has retained secretions in the right middle lobe. Which position uses gravity best to drain this lobe?

options.A: Lying prone with the foot of the bed lowered
options.B: Lying on the left side with the foot of the bed raised
options.C: Sitting upright and leaning forward
options.D: Lying on the right side with the head of the bed raised

questions.correct_text: Lying on the left side with the foot of the bed raised
explanation: Drainage positions put the affected segment on top and the bronchus pointing downward.
The right middle lobe drains with the client tilted head down and turned onto the opposite side.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Postural drainage for the right middle lobe

questions.question: A client on postoperative day 1 is agitated and pulling at the IV and the dressing. The nurse is considering a restraint. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Apply wrist restraints to protect the lines
options.B: Give a PRN sedative before any assessment
options.C: Move the client to a room near the desk and watch right now as planned right now
options.D: Assess for hypoxia, pain, a full bladder, and other causes of agitation

questions.correct_text: Assess for hypoxia, pain, a full bladder, and other causes of agitation
explanation: Agitation often signals a treatable problem, such as low oxygen, pain, or retention.
Restraints and sedatives hide the problem and add risk.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with a head injury from a fall is unresponsive. The provider asks the nurse to test the oculocephalic (doll's eyes) reflex. What should the nurse confirm first?

options.A: That a cervical spine injury has been ruled out
options.B: That the client's family has arrived
options.C: That the room lights are off
options.D: That the client has eaten

questions.correct_text: That a cervical spine injury has been ruled out
explanation: The test turns the head, and this movement can damage an unstable neck.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A 3-month-old is irritable and vomiting, with a bulging fontanel and retinal hemorrhages. The caregiver reports no injury. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Ask the caregiver to leave the room until the physician arrives right now at this time
options.B: Suspect abusive head trauma, support the infant, and report per mandated reporting law
options.C: Treat the vomiting as a feeding problem and discharge
options.D: Wait for the scan results before considering any report

questions.correct_text: Suspect abusive head trauma, support the infant, and report per mandated reporting law
explanation: This pattern of findings with no explanation suggests shaking injury.
Mandated reporters report reasonable suspicion without waiting for proof.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Infant with signs of abusive head trauma

questions.question: A client with a valid living will refusing CPR has a cardiac arrest. The spouse says, "Do everything. I do not care what the paper says." What should the nurse do?

options.A: Follow the client's documented wishes and offer support to the spouse
options.B: Wait for the family to agree before acting
options.C: Begin CPR and ask the provider to stop later
options.D: Begin CPR, as the spouse is the legal next of kin for the moment for now

questions.correct_text: Follow the client's documented wishes and offer support to the spouse
explanation: A valid directive reflects the client's own decision, and a family member cannot override it.
Support for the spouse and a review through ethics address the conflict.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Advance directive conflicts with a relative

questions.question: On postoperative day 1 after colostomy creation, the stoma is dark purple-black, dry, and cool. How should the nurse interpret this finding?

options.A: A sign of mild anemia
options.B: Compromised blood supply that needs immediate evaluation
options.C: Normal early swelling that will resolve
options.D: Dryness from the appliance that needs more skin barrier today

questions.correct_text: Compromised blood supply that needs immediate evaluation
explanation: A healthy stoma is pink to red and moist.
Dark purple to black indicates ischemia and risks necrosis.
Swelling is expected, but color change is not.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Twenty minutes into a red cell transfusion, a client develops hives and itching. Vital signs are unchanged, and the client has no dyspnea. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Remove the IV and apply ice to the skin
options.B: Increase the rate to finish before the reaction worsens right now today
options.C: Continue the transfusion at the same rate and monitor
options.D: Stop the transfusion, keep the IV open with saline, and recheck the vital signs

questions.correct_text: Stop the transfusion, keep the IV open with saline, and recheck the vital signs
explanation: Hives without other signs suggest a mild allergic reaction, and the transfusion is paused.
Treatment follows orders, and the transfusion may resume only as the protocol allows.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Order: 75 mg/m2 IV. The client's body surface area is 1.8 m2. What dose should the nurse verify?

options.A: 270 mg
options.C: 135 mg
options.D: 75 mg

questions.correct_text: 135 mg
explanation: 41.7 results from dividing instead of multiplying.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Chemotherapy dose by body surface area

questions.question: A 1,000 mL bag of fluid was hung at 0600 and runs at 125 mL/hr. How many mL remain at 1330?

options.A: 63 mL
options.B: 188 mL
options.C: 125 mL
options.D: 937 mL

questions.correct_text: 63 mL
explanation: From 0600 to 1330 is 7.5 hours, and 7.5 x 125 = 937.5 mL infused.
1,000 - 937.5 = 62.5, or about 63 mL, remains.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: On day 2 of admission, a client has yawning, runny nose, dilated pupils, goose bumps, abdominal cramps, and diarrhea. Vital signs show mild tachycardia. Which condition does the nurse suspect?

options.A: Viral gastroenteritis
options.B: Alcohol withdrawal with seizures
options.C: Allergic reaction to a medication
options.D: Opioid withdrawal

questions.correct_text: Opioid withdrawal
explanation: Dilated pupils, goose bumps, yawning, and a runny nose with cramps are typical of opioid withdrawal.
Alcohol withdrawal causes tremor, sweating, and hallucinations.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: On day 5 after a bowel resection, a client has a temperature of 38.9 C, HR 118, a rigid abdomen, and a white blood cell count of 19,000/mm3. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Advance the diet and monitor the temperature for the moment right now as planned
options.B: Keep the client NPO and prepare for urgent evaluation of a possible leak
options.C: Apply heat to the abdomen for comfort
options.D: Give a stool softener and encourage walking

questions.correct_text: Keep the client NPO and prepare for urgent evaluation of a possible leak
explanation: Fever, tachycardia, a rigid abdomen, and a high white count suggest bowel contents leaking into the abdomen.
Feeding, laxatives, or heat can worsen the problem.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client takes lithium at 0800 and 2000. When should a routine blood level be drawn?

options.A: 2 hours after the dose
options.B: 30 minutes after the dose
options.C: At any time, as the level does not change
options.D: About 12 hours after the last dose, before the next dose

questions.correct_text: About 12 hours after the last dose, before the next dose
explanation: A trough level 12 hours after the dose gives the most reliable reading.
A peak level is misleading and can seem toxic.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with long-term alcohol use has tremor, hyperactive reflexes, muscle cramps, and a magnesium of 1.0 mg/dL. What should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: IV magnesium replacement and seizure precautions
options.B: A sedative for the tremor
options.C: Fluid restriction and a diuretic
options.D: Oral calcium as the sole treatment

questions.correct_text: IV magnesium replacement and seizure precautions
explanation: Low magnesium causes neuromuscular irritability and can cause seizures and torsades.
Replacement is given with monitoring.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: The nurse needs to hang a scheduled IV antibiotic, call the pharmacy, chart, and answer a client's family. A client suddenly has slurred speech and facial droop. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Call the pharmacy about the missing dose today for now
options.B: Assess the client and activate the stroke response
options.C: Hang the scheduled antibiotic
options.D: Complete the charting for the shift

questions.correct_text: Assess the client and activate the stroke response
explanation: New neurologic changes may be a stroke, and treatment depends on time.
The other tasks can wait.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: New speech change while other tasks are pending

questions.question: An 80-year-old client on postoperative day 2 has stable vital signs and has been awakened for checks at 0000, 0200, and 0400. The client is now confused at night. Which plan best promotes sleep?

options.A: Group care activities and allow at least 4 uninterrupted hours of sleep when the client is stable
options.B: Continue checks every 2 hours to detect any change early
options.C: Give a sedative-hypnotic at 2200 to make sure the client sleeps through the night right now as planned
options.D: Keep the lights on and the television running so the client stays oriented

questions.correct_text: Group care activities and allow at least 4 uninterrupted hours of sleep when the client is stable
explanation: Broken sleep and sedative drugs both raise the risk of delirium in older adults.
Clustering care and space between checks protect sleep while safety is kept.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Protecting sleep in a client at risk for delirium

questions.question: A client received IM epinephrine for anaphylaxis to a medication. After 30 minutes, the client feels well, and vital signs are normal. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Discharge the client now, as the reaction has resolved
options.B: Remove the IV and send the client home with a prescription
options.C: Stop monitoring and let the client sleep
options.D: Continue to observe for several hours; symptoms can return

questions.correct_text: Continue to observe for several hours; symptoms can return
explanation: A second wave of symptoms can occur hours after the first.
Observation of 4 to 6 hours or longer is common.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A 15-year-old has sudden severe pain in the left scrotum, nausea, and a high-riding, tender testicle. The pain began 2 hours ago. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Arrange immediate evaluation, as this may be torsion that needs surgery within hours
options.B: Observe for a day to see if the pain resolves at this time
options.C: Treat the pain as a routine urinary infection
options.D: Apply heat and give an oral analgesic

questions.correct_text: Arrange immediate evaluation, as this may be torsion that needs surgery within hours
explanation: Twisting of the testicle cuts off its blood supply, and tissue is lost after about 6 hours.
Delay risks loss of the testicle.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: After resuscitation from cardiac arrest, a client's ABG shows pH 7.18, PaCO2 62 mm Hg, and HCO3 17 mEq/L. Which interpretation is correct?

options.A: Respiratory acidosis with partial metabolic compensation
options.B: Respiratory acidosis with full metabolic compensation
options.C: Combined respiratory and metabolic acidosis
options.D: Metabolic acidosis with partial respiratory compensation

questions.correct_text: Combined respiratory and metabolic acidosis
explanation: A high PaCO2 points to respiratory acidosis, and a low HCO3 points to metabolic acidosis; both push the pH down.
True compensation moves the other value in the opposite direction of the primary problem (HCO3 up or PaCO2 down), which is not seen here.
Hypoventilation plus lactic acidosis is typical after arrest.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client taking furosemide and digoxin has a potassium of 2.7 mEq/L, and the monitor shows new premature ventricular beats. Four orders are written. Which order should the nurse question?

options.A: Potassium chloride 40 mEq in 100 mL IV over 30 minutes by peripheral line
options.B: Potassium chloride 10 mEq in 100 mL IV over 1 hour with continuous cardiac monitoring
options.C: Hold the next digoxin dose until the repeat potassium result is back
options.D: Repeat the serum potassium and magnesium levels after the infusion ends

questions.correct_text: Potassium chloride 40 mEq in 100 mL IV over 30 minutes by peripheral line
explanation: 40 mEq over 30 minutes is 80 mEq/hr, far above the usual 10 mEq/hr peripheral limit, and risks cardiac arrest.
Slow, monitored replacement is the expected plan for a potassium this low with ectopy.
Holding digoxin is reasonable because low potassium increases digoxin toxicity; rechecking magnesium is reasonable because low magnesium keeps potassium low.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client in the recovery phase of acute kidney injury now produces 4 liters of urine daily. What should the nurse monitor most closely?

options.A: For fluid overload alone, as the kidneys have recovered fully
options.B: For nothing unusual, as this is a normal finding
options.C: Fluid balance and serum electrolytes, as large losses can cause dehydration and low potassium
options.D: For rising potassium, as in the early phase

questions.correct_text: Fluid balance and serum electrolytes, as large losses can cause dehydration and low potassium
explanation: The recovering kidneys cannot yet concentrate urine, which causes large losses of water and electrolytes.
The client may need replacement of fluid and electrolytes.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Recovery phase of acute kidney injury

questions.question: A farmer has excess saliva, tearing, sweating, a heart rate of 44, and small pupils after pesticide exposure. Which drug should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Naloxone
options.B: Vitamin K
options.C: Glucagon
options.D: Atropine

questions.correct_text: Atropine
explanation: The pattern suggests an overload of acetylcholine from an organophosphate.
Atropine blocks the effects on the heart and secretions.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client after prostate surgery has continuous bladder irrigation. The outflow is bright red with clots, and the client has bladder pain. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Increase the irrigation rate as ordered and keep the catheter draining freely
options.B: Remove the catheter to inspect the bladder
options.C: Clamp the outflow tubing
options.D: Slow the irrigation to let the bladder rest at this time today for now as planned

questions.correct_text: Increase the irrigation rate as ordered and keep the catheter draining freely
explanation: Bright red outflow with clots means active bleeding, and faster irrigation prevents clots from blocking the catheter.
A blocked catheter makes the bladder distend and bleed more.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Bright red bladder drainage with clots

questions.question: A nurse witnesses a client signing a consent form. The client asks, "What are the chances this will not work?" The nurse does not know. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Have the client sign and write the question on the side of the form
options.B: Tell the client to sign now and ask the provider questions afterward
options.C: Give an estimate based on the nurse's experience with similar clients
options.D: Stop the process and ask the provider to give the information first

questions.correct_text: Stop the process and ask the provider to give the information first
explanation: Informed consent requires that the provider explain risks, benefits, and alternatives and answer questions.
The nurse witnesses the signature and protects the client's right to understand.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: After an opioid overdose, a client has RR 6 and an ABG of pH 7.21, PaCO2 68, and HCO3 25. How should the nurse interpret this?

options.A: Compensated respiratory acidosis typical of chronic lung disease for now
options.B: Acute respiratory acidosis with no compensation; support ventilation
options.C: Metabolic acidosis from lactic acid
options.D: Respiratory alkalosis from anxiety

questions.correct_text: Acute respiratory acidosis with no compensation; support ventilation
explanation: A high PaCO2 with a low pH shows hypoventilation, and a normal bicarbonate shows the kidneys have not had time to compensate.
The treatment is ventilation support and reversal of the opioid.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with asthma receives albuterol by nebulizer. Afterward, HR rises from 88 to 148, and the client has tremor and feels anxious. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Give a sedative for the anxiety
options.B: Reassure the client that this is expected and give another dose for the moment
options.C: Repeat the treatment in 15 minutes for better effect
options.D: Stop the treatment and assess the heart rate, rhythm, and breathing

questions.correct_text: Stop the treatment and assess the heart rate, rhythm, and breathing
explanation: Albuterol can cause a fast heart rate and tremor, and a large rise is a concern.
More drug adds risk.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with a head injury has a mean arterial pressure of 80 mm Hg and an intracranial pressure of 25 mm Hg. What is the cerebral perfusion pressure, and what does it mean?

options.A: 55 mm Hg; it is below the usual goal of 60 or more and needs intervention
options.B: 105 mm Hg; it is high and needs no action
options.C: 55 mm Hg; it is within the usual goal
options.D: 3.2 mm Hg; it is dangerously low

questions.correct_text: 55 mm Hg; it is below the usual goal of 60 or more and needs intervention
explanation: Cerebral perfusion pressure = mean arterial pressure - intracranial pressure = 80 - 25 = 55.
A value under about 60 risks brain ischemia.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A child weighs 20 kg. The drug's maximum safe dose is 100 mg/kg/day. The order is 600 mg every 6 hours. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Give the dose and watch for side effects
options.B: Give half the dose and call the provider
options.C: Hold the dose, as it gives 120 mg/kg/day, above the safe limit
options.D: Give the dose, as it is within the safe range as planned as planned

questions.correct_text: Hold the dose, as it gives 120 mg/kg/day, above the safe limit
explanation: The total is 600 x 4 = 2,400 mg per day, which is 120 mg/kg/day, above the limit.
A nurse does not change a dose without an order.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Daily dose check in a child

questions.question: A client with obstructive sleep apnea is on postoperative day 1 and receiving opioids by PCA. Which plan is safest?

options.A: Use the client's own CPAP when sleeping, keep the head elevated, and monitor oxygen and breathing closely
options.B: Keep the client flat and reduce monitoring so the client can rest
options.C: Avoid CPAP, as the client is alert and has no airway problem
options.D: Give a sedative at night to help the client sleep through the night today

questions.correct_text: Use the client's own CPAP when sleeping, keep the head elevated, and monitor oxygen and breathing closely
explanation: Opioids and sleep relax the airway and breathing drive, which is dangerous in sleep apnea.
CPAP, elevation, and close monitoring reduce the risk.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: After 3 days of bed rest, a client is to walk for the first time. Place the actions in order: 1 Dangle at the edge of the bed. 2 Raise the head of the bed gradually. 3 Stand with assistance. 4 Walk with assistance. Which order is correct?
explanation: The body adjusts to upright positions in steps, which lowers the risk of a sudden drop in blood pressure.
Raising the head, then dangling, then standing, then walking gives time to check for dizziness at each step.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A newborn weighs 8 lb 6 oz. What is the weight in kilograms? (Round to the nearest tenth.)

options.B: 3.6 kg
options.C: 3.8 kg
options.D: 4.2 kg

questions.correct_text: 3.8 kg
explanation: 8 lb 6 oz = 8.375 lb.
3.6 kg ignores the ounces.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A child swallowed many iron tablets and has vomiting, bloody stool, and metabolic acidosis. Which drug should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Naloxone
options.B: Fomepizole for now
options.C: Flumazenil
options.D: Deferoxamine

questions.correct_text: Deferoxamine
explanation: Deferoxamine binds iron so that it can be excreted in the urine.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A provider orders 25 g of dextrose for severe hypoglycemia. The vial is 50% dextrose. How many mL should the nurse give?

options.A: 100 mL
options.C: 50 mL
options.D: 25 mL

questions.correct_text: 50 mL
explanation: A 50% solution has 50 g per 100 mL, or 0.5 g per mL.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client standing at the bedside for the first time after surgery says, "I feel dizzy." The skin is pale, and the knees begin to buckle. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Support the arms and walk the client back to bed today as planned
options.B: Hold the client upright and call for a chair
options.C: Offer sips of water and wait
options.D: Lower the client to the floor while protecting the head

questions.correct_text: Lower the client to the floor while protecting the head
explanation: Trying to hold a falling client risks injury to both people.
Controlled lowering to the floor protects the head and prevents a fall.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client taking atorvastatin reports severe muscle pain and weakness and has dark brown urine. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Hold the next dose and prepare to check a creatine kinase level
options.B: Give the next dose and add a muscle relaxant
options.C: Reassure the client that muscle ache is a normal effect
options.D: Apply heat to the muscles and recheck in the morning

questions.correct_text: Hold the next dose and prepare to check a creatine kinase level
explanation: Severe pain with dark urine suggests muscle breakdown, which can injure the kidneys.
The drug is held until the cause is confirmed.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Statin with muscle pain and dark urine

questions.question: A client returns from a bronchoscopy with topical anesthesia of the throat. The client asks for water. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Give sips of water at once, as the client is awake and alert
options.B: Give ice chips, as they are considered safe at any time
options.C: Give a full glass of water so the throat is soothed
options.D: Hold oral intake until the gag reflex has returned

questions.correct_text: Hold oral intake until the gag reflex has returned
explanation: The anesthetic blocks the gag reflex, so swallowing is unsafe and can cause aspiration.
The return of the gag reflex is checked before any intake.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A bag contains 40 mEq of potassium chloride in 500 mL and runs at 125 mL/hr. How many mEq of potassium does the client receive each hour?

options.A: 40 mEq/hr
options.B: 5 mEq/hr
options.C: 10 mEq/hr
options.D: 20 mEq/hr

questions.correct_text: 10 mEq/hr
explanation: The bag has 80 mEq per liter, and 125 mL is one-eighth of a liter.
80 / 8 = 10 mEq/hr, which is the usual limit for peripheral infusion.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Potassium delivered per hour from a bag

questions.question: Which laboratory result should the nurse report first?

options.A: WBC 11,000/mm3 in a client after surgery
options.B: Glucose 190 mg/dL in a client who has diabetes and a meal tray at this time
options.C: Hemoglobin 9.0 g/dL in a client who is stable and walking
options.D: Potassium 6.4 mEq/L in a client with peaked T waves on the monitor

questions.correct_text: Potassium 6.4 mEq/L in a client with peaked T waves on the monitor
explanation: High potassium with ECG changes can cause fatal arrhythmia.
The other values are mildly abnormal and expected.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Which laboratory result to report first

questions.question: A client with metastatic breast cancer has new severe back pain, weakness in both legs, and difficulty starting urination. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Keep the client lying flat and arrange urgent imaging and treatment
options.B: Apply heat and give an oral analgesic
options.C: Document the findings and reassess tomorrow for the moment
options.D: Encourage walking to loosen the muscles

questions.correct_text: Keep the client lying flat and arrange urgent imaging and treatment
explanation: The symptoms suggest compression of the spinal cord by a tumor, and delay can cause permanent paralysis.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: New back pain with leg weakness in cancer

questions.question: A client took an overdose of a beta blocker and has a heart rate of 36, BP 70/40, and a glucose of 58 mg/dL. Which drug should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Protamine sulfate
options.B: Naloxone
options.C: Flumazenil
options.D: Glucagon

questions.correct_text: Glucagon
explanation: Glucagon raises heart rate and contraction through a different pathway from the blocked receptors.
It also raises glucose.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A drug has a half-life of 8 hours. About how long will it take to reach steady state with regular dosing?

options.A: About 16 hours
options.B: About 40 hours
options.C: About 8 hours
options.D: About 80 hours

questions.correct_text: About 40 hours
explanation: Steady state is reached after about five half-lives.
5 x 8 hours = 40 hours.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Ten minutes into a red cell transfusion, a client has chills, flank pain, BP 88/50, and a temperature of 38.8 C. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Continue at a slow rate and recheck the vital signs every 5 minutes
options.B: Slow the transfusion rate and give the PRN acetaminophen and diphenhydramine
options.C: Stop the transfusion and flush the same tubing with 0.9% sodium chloride
options.D: Stop the transfusion and infuse 0.9% sodium chloride through new tubing

questions.correct_text: Stop the transfusion and infuse 0.9% sodium chloride through new tubing
explanation: Flank pain and hypotension point to a hemolytic reaction, not a mild fever reaction.
The infusion is stopped immediately, and saline is run through new tubing so no more blood enters.
Flushing the old tubing pushes residual blood into the client.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: At 1000 a client receives morphine 4 mg IV for pain. At 1030 a consent form for surgery is brought for signature. The client is drowsy, answers slowly, and cannot state the surgical risks. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Obtain verbal consent now and have the client sign the form later today
options.B: Delay the signing until the client is alert enough to understand the information
options.C: Ask the spouse to sign the consent form in place of the client right now
options.D: Have the client sign and witness the signature after confirming the client states their name

questions.correct_text: Delay the signing until the client is alert enough to understand the information
explanation: Valid consent requires that the client understands the information, which sedation can impair.
The client is expected to regain capacity, and the procedure is not an emergency, so the client signs later.
A surrogate signs only when the client lacks capacity and cannot regain it in time.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with type 1 diabetes is NPO for surgery at 0800. Insulin glargine 30 units is due at 0700, and the glucose is 118 mg/dL. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Give the insulin together with 50% dextrose given by IV push right now
options.B: Hold the insulin until the client returns from surgery and is eating
options.C: Give the basal insulin as ordered and monitor the glucose often
options.D: Hold the insulin, as the client is NPO for the planned surgery this morning

questions.correct_text: Give the basal insulin as ordered and monitor the glucose often
explanation: A client with type 1 diabetes still needs basal insulin when fasting, and omission can lead to ketoacidosis.
Glucose is checked often during the fast, and any dose change comes from an order.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with disseminated varicella (chickenpox) is in an airborne isolation room. Which nurse should NOT be assigned to this client?

options.A: A pregnant nurse with a documented positive varicella antibody titer
options.B: A first-trimester nurse with no record of chickenpox or vaccination
options.C: A nurse with two documented doses of varicella vaccine given years ago
options.D: A nurse who recovered from an episode of shingles during the past year

questions.correct_text: A first-trimester nurse with no record of chickenpox or vaccination
explanation: Only nurses with proven immunity should care for this client, and a nonimmune pregnant nurse risks serious harm to herself and the fetus.
Pregnancy alone does not exclude a nurse who has documented immunity.
Vaccination, a positive titer, and a prior shingles episode all show immunity.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Staffing for a client with varicella

questions.question: A client has right lower abdominal pain, nausea, and a temperature of 37.9 C, and asks for a heating pad. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Apply a hot water bottle and observe the skin
options.B: Apply the heating pad on a low setting for 20 minutes at this time
options.C: Give a laxative to relieve the cramping
options.D: Withhold heat, as it can increase the risk of rupture, and keep the client NPO

questions.correct_text: Withhold heat, as it can increase the risk of rupture, and keep the client NPO
explanation: These findings suggest appendicitis, and heat can raise the risk that the appendix ruptures.
A laxative also raises the risk.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has sharp chest pain that worsens when lying back and on deep breathing and eases when sitting forward. A scratchy sound is heard over the left sternal border. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: A pneumothorax, so the nurse lays the client flat
options.B: A muscle strain, so the nurse applies heat
options.C: Pericarditis, so the nurse helps the client sit forward and monitors for signs of fluid around the heart
options.D: Heartburn, so the nurse gives an antacid and observes as planned

questions.correct_text: Pericarditis, so the nurse helps the client sit forward and monitors for signs of fluid around the heart
explanation: Pain that changes with position and a friction rub indicate inflammation of the heart sac.
Fluid can build up and cause tamponade, so the nurse watches for falling pressure and distended neck veins.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A person found outdoors has a core temperature of 28 C, HR 40, and slow shallow breathing. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Place the person in a hot bath to rewarm the body quickly right now
options.B: Rub the arms and legs vigorously to restore the circulation to the limbs for the moment
options.C: Give a hot drink by mouth to raise the core temperature from within
options.D: Handle gently, prevent more heat loss, and start core rewarming per protocol

questions.correct_text: Handle gently, prevent more heat loss, and start core rewarming per protocol
explanation: Rough handling can trigger ventricular fibrillation in a cold heart.
Core rewarming is safer than rewarming the limbs first.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with type 1 diabetes has vomiting, a glucose of 480 mg/dL, sodium 138, chloride 98, and bicarbonate 10 mEq/L. What is the anion gap and its meaning?

options.A: 12; a normal gap from bicarbonate loss
options.B: 20; a gap caused by chloride loss
options.C: 30; a high gap, consistent with ketoacid buildup
options.D: 30; a normal finding in diabetes

questions.correct_text: 30; a high gap, consistent with ketoacid buildup
explanation: Anion gap = sodium - (chloride + bicarbonate) = 138 - 108 = 30.
A normal gap is about 8 to 12, so 30 shows added unmeasured acids such as ketones.
Bicarbonate loss from diarrhea gives a normal gap with high chloride.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with type 1 diabetes has a fasting glucose of 240 mg/dL. The provider considers increasing the evening NPH insulin. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Give a correction dose each night without further data at this time today
options.B: Check the glucose at about 0300 to find out whether the morning value follows a low
options.C: Skip the evening insulin to see what happens
options.D: Increase the evening insulin dose as planned

questions.correct_text: Check the glucose at about 0300 to find out whether the morning value follows a low
explanation: A high morning value can follow a night low, when hormones raise glucose in response.
The 0300 value separates this from the dawn phenomenon before any dose change.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Which client should the nurse assess first?

options.A: A client 2 hours after femoral artery catheterization with a firm 6 cm groin swelling, BP 98/58, and HR 112
options.B: A client after catheterization who has a small bruise at the site and a pulse of 74
options.C: A client 6 hours after cardiac catheterization with a flat groin site, BP 128/76, and mild back ache
options.D: A client after catheterization who reports hunger and asks when the bed rest order ends

questions.correct_text: A client 2 hours after femoral artery catheterization with a firm 6 cm groin swelling, BP 98/58, and HR 112
explanation: A growing firm swelling with falling BP and rising heart rate suggests active bleeding into the thigh or abdomen.
The other clients have expected findings after the procedure.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client receives 5% dextrose with 0.45% sodium chloride containing 40 mEq/L of potassium chloride at 150 mL/hr. How many mEq of potassium does the client receive each hour?

options.A: 4 mEq/hr
options.B: 6 mEq/hr
options.C: 40 mEq/hr
options.D: 2.7 mEq/hr

questions.correct_text: 6 mEq/hr
explanation: 150 mL is 0.15 L, and 0.15 x 40 = 6 mEq.
This is within the usual 10 mEq/hr limit for peripheral infusion.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A provider orders normal saline IM PRN for pain for a client with chronic pain and writes "do not tell the client it is saline." What should the nurse do?

options.A: Give the injection per the order and chart it as an analgesic given for chronic pain
options.B: Give the injection as ordered and leave responsibility for the order with the provider
options.C: Give the injection as ordered, reassess the pain level after 30 minutes, and document the response
options.D: Decline to give the injection and raise the concern with the provider and nurse manager

questions.correct_text: Decline to give the injection and raise the concern with the provider and nurse manager
explanation: Giving a saline injection while implying it is a pain medication violates honesty and informed consent.
A valid order does not remove the nurse's duty to question an unethical order.
Charting it as an analgesic is a false record.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has had profuse watery diarrhea for 3 days and now has deep, rapid breathing, weakness, and HR 112. Which ABG result is most consistent with this client's condition?

options.A: pH 7.28, PaCO2 26 mm Hg, HCO3 12 mEq/L
options.B: pH 7.28, PaCO2 56 mm Hg, HCO3 26 mEq/L
options.C: pH 7.52, PaCO2 30 mm Hg, HCO3 24 mEq/L
options.D: pH 7.50, PaCO2 48 mm Hg, HCO3 36 mEq/L

questions.correct_text: pH 7.28, PaCO2 26 mm Hg, HCO3 12 mEq/L
explanation: Bicarbonate loss in stool causes metabolic acidosis (low pH, low HCO3).
Deep, rapid breathing blows off CO2, so PaCO2 is low; the pH is still acidic, so compensation is partial.
The other results show respiratory acidosis, respiratory alkalosis, and metabolic alkalosis.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: At a visit, an 8-month-old still shows a strong startle (Moro) reflex when the head is dropped slightly. What should the nurse conclude?

options.A: This is normal at 8 months and needs no follow-up
options.B: This shows normal development of the nervous system for the moment
options.C: The reflex normally disappears by about 4 to 6 months, so the finding needs a developmental evaluation
options.D: This is a sign that the infant is hungry

questions.correct_text: The reflex normally disappears by about 4 to 6 months, so the finding needs a developmental evaluation
explanation: A Moro reflex that persists past about 6 months suggests a neurologic problem.
The finding is reported for follow-up.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: An 82-year-old admitted with dehydration has bruises in different stages of healing on the upper arms. Her son answers every question and refuses to leave the room. The client says quietly, "I fell." What should the nurse do?

options.A: Document the bruises in detail and reassess for new injuries over the next 48 hours
options.B: Interview the client alone and report the suspicion per mandated reporting policy
options.C: Ask the son to explain each of the bruises while the client is present
options.D: Wait until the client confirms the abuse before submitting a report to the agency

questions.correct_text: Interview the client alone and report the suspicion per mandated reporting policy
explanation: Reasonable suspicion triggers mandated reporting, and the client's confirmation is not required.
A private interview protects the client, while confronting the suspected abuser can escalate risk.
Waiting or watching delays protection of a vulnerable adult.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Order: levothyroxine 0.088 mg by mouth daily. Available tablets are 44 mcg. How many tablets should the nurse give?

options.A: 2 tablets
options.B: 0.5 tablet
options.C: 1 tablet
options.D: 4 tablets

questions.correct_text: 2 tablets
explanation: 88 / 44 = 2 tablets.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client hospitalized with major depression was withdrawn and flat for 8 days. Today the client is calm and cheerful, gives a watch and books to staff, and says, "I have everything figured out. Thanks for everything." What should the nurse do?

options.A: Reassure the client and recheck mood at the next shift
options.B: Accept the gifts politely and document the improved mood
options.C: Ask directly about suicidal thoughts and a plan, and start safety precautions
options.D: Compliment the improvement and ask the provider about reducing observation as planned

questions.correct_text: Ask directly about suicidal thoughts and a plan, and start safety precautions
explanation: Sudden calm with giving away possessions and farewell language can signal a decision to die.
Direct questions do not plant the idea, and precautions protect the client while risk is assessed.
Reading the calm as improvement and lowering observation is a dangerous error.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client 3 days after hip surgery suddenly develops chest pain, dyspnea, and SpO2 86%. HR is 124. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Have the client walk around the unit slowly to improve the oxygenation
options.B: Raise the head of the bed, apply oxygen, and stay with the client
options.C: Apply a heating pad to the chest to relieve the pain and relax the muscles
options.D: Give the PRN sedative to reduce anxiety and slow the breathing rate down

questions.correct_text: Raise the head of the bed, apply oxygen, and stay with the client
explanation: The pattern suggests a clot in the pulmonary artery.
Oxygen and a position that eases breathing support the client while help arrives.
Walking can move more clot, and sedation hides worsening.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Nursing action for suspected pulmonary embolism

questions.question: A client has been NPO on broad-spectrum antibiotics for 10 days and has an INR of 2.8. The client takes no anticoagulant. What does the nurse suspect?

options.A: A reaction to the antibiotic that needs a different class of drug
options.B: Liver failure that needs an immediate transplant evaluation
options.C: A normal laboratory change after bed rest
options.D: A vitamin K deficiency, so the nurse anticipates vitamin K replacement

questions.correct_text: A vitamin K deficiency, so the nurse anticipates vitamin K replacement
explanation: Gut bacteria make part of the body's vitamin K, and antibiotics plus fasting lower it.
A raised INR in a client without warfarin supports the diagnosis.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client who had a head injury 12 hours ago has a sodium of 129 mEq/L and a declining level of consciousness. The provider writes four IV fluid orders. Which order should the nurse question?

options.A: 3% sodium chloride by pump at the protocol rate
options.B: 0.9% sodium chloride with 20 mEq/L potassium at 100 mL/hr
options.C: 0.45% sodium chloride infused at 100 mL/hr by pump
options.D: 0.9% sodium chloride infused at 100 mL/hr by pump

questions.correct_text: 0.45% sodium chloride infused at 100 mL/hr by pump
explanation: Hypotonic fluid moves water into brain cells and can raise intracranial pressure.
Isotonic saline is the usual choice, and hypertonic saline is used per protocol for symptomatic hyponatremia or raised pressure.
Potassium is acceptable here because no kidney impairment is stated.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client says, "The nurses are putting poison in my food." Which response is best?

options.A: Why do you think the nurses would want to poison you or any other client?
options.B: You are right to worry, so I will order a different tray for your next meal
options.C: That is not true; the food is prepared safely by trained kitchen staff here at this time
options.D: I know this feels real to you, but I do not believe it; I will stay with you

questions.correct_text: I know this feels real to you, but I do not believe it; I will stay with you
explanation: The nurse states a different view without arguing and offers support to reduce fear.
Debate invites more defense of the belief, and agreement reinforces it.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with a tricyclic antidepressant overdose has a wide QRS complex on the ECG and a seizure. Which drug should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Atropine
options.B: Acetylcysteine for now
options.C: Sodium bicarbonate
options.D: Flumazenil

questions.correct_text: Sodium bicarbonate
explanation: Bicarbonate narrows the QRS and limits heart toxicity.
Flumazenil can worsen seizures in this setting.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with chest pain has ST elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, BP 84/50, distended neck veins, and clear lung sounds. What should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Avoiding nitroglycerin and giving IV fluids, as the right ventricle may be involved
options.B: Giving nitroglycerin to relieve the chest pain
options.C: Giving a diuretic for the neck vein distention
options.D: Giving a beta blocker to slow the heart rate

questions.correct_text: Avoiding nitroglycerin and giving IV fluids, as the right ventricle may be involved
explanation: Right ventricular involvement makes the heart depend on preload, and nitrates can drop the pressure sharply.
Fluids support the filling of the right side.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client reports flashes of light and then a curtain-like shadow across part of the vision in one eye. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Encourage the client to read to test the vision
options.B: Apply a warm compress and observe
options.C: Keep the client calm and still, avoid straining, and arrange urgent eye evaluation
options.D: Have the client perform vigorous exercises to loosen the retina at this time for now

questions.correct_text: Keep the client calm and still, avoid straining, and arrange urgent eye evaluation
explanation: A curtain-like loss of vision suggests the retina is peeling away from the back of the eye.
Rest limits further detachment until surgery.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has a narrow-complex regular rhythm at 180/min, is alert, and has a BP of 118/74. What should the nurse anticipate first?

options.A: A fluid restriction and observation
options.B: A vagal maneuver, such as bearing down, before medication is used
options.C: Chest compressions
options.D: Immediate defibrillation

questions.correct_text: A vagal maneuver, such as bearing down, before medication is used
explanation: A stable client with a fast supraventricular rhythm may convert with a vagal maneuver.
Medication follows if the maneuver fails.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Vancomycin 1 g is ordered every 12 hours at 0800 and 2000, starting at 0800 on day 1. When should the trough level be drawn?

options.A: At 0930 on day 1, 90 minutes after the first dose
options.B: At 0800 on day 3, after the fifth dose
options.C: At 1930 on day 2, before the fourth dose
options.D: At 2100 on day 1, after the second dose

questions.correct_text: At 1930 on day 2, before the fourth dose
explanation: A trough is the lowest level and is drawn within 30 minutes before a dose, usually before the fourth dose when steady state is reached.
Draws after a dose give a peak or a random level.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: The parenteral nutrition bag is empty at 0200, and the next bag from the pharmacy will arrive in 2 hours. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Hang 0.9% sodium chloride at a keep-open rate and check the glucose in 4 hours
options.B: Hang 10% dextrose at the same rate and check the glucose
options.C: Hang 5% dextrose in 0.45% sodium chloride at twice the rate to catch up
options.D: Stop the line and wait for the pharmacy bag without any other fluid

questions.correct_text: Hang 10% dextrose at the same rate and check the glucose
explanation: A sudden stop of a high-dextrose feeding can cause rebound hypoglycemia from the high insulin level.
Dextrose at a similar rate bridges the gap, and glucose checks confirm safety.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client receives NPH insulin at 0800. When is the greatest risk of hypoglycemia?

options.A: Between about 1200 and 2000
options.B: Not until the following morning
options.C: Between 0800 and 0830
options.D: Between 0830 and 0930

questions.correct_text: Between about 1200 and 2000
explanation: NPH has an onset of 1 to 2 hours and a peak of about 4 to 12 hours.
Meals and snacks are timed to cover this period.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client will be transported with a portable E cylinder reading 1,800 psi at 4 L/min. The cylinder factor is 0.28, and a safe residual of 500 psi is required. About how many minutes of oxygen are available?

options.A: 364 minutes
options.B: 126 minutes
options.C: 91 minutes
options.D: 23 minutes

questions.correct_text: 91 minutes
explanation: Usable pressure: 1,800 - 500 = 1,300 psi.
Duration: (1,300 x 0.28) / 4 = 91 minutes.
126 minutes ignores the safe residual, and 364 skips division by flow.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client taking sertraline starts St John's wort. The client now has agitation, tremor, sweating, HR 122, temperature 38.7 C, and muscle jerks in the legs. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Give acetaminophen and encourage rest
options.B: Suspect serotonin syndrome, hold the supplement, and monitor temperature and heart rhythm
options.C: Reassure the client that the symptoms are anxiety
options.D: Increase the sertraline dose to calm the symptoms for the moment today

questions.correct_text: Suspect serotonin syndrome, hold the supplement, and monitor temperature and heart rhythm
explanation: Combining two serotonin-increasing agents can cause toxicity with fever, agitation, and muscle jerks.
This is an emergency that needs treatment.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: The tray has arrived, and rapid-acting insulin is due with the meal. The client is shaky and sweating, and the glucose is 52 mg/dL. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Have the client eat the meal and give the insulin afterward at this time for the moment
options.B: Give half the insulin dose with the meal
options.C: Treat the low glucose with fast-acting carbohydrate and recheck before giving insulin
options.D: Give the insulin now so the meal and the dose are matched

questions.correct_text: Treat the low glucose with fast-acting carbohydrate and recheck before giving insulin
explanation: A glucose of 52 mg/dL is hypoglycemia, and insulin would worsen it.
The glucose is corrected and rechecked before any dose decision.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with asthma is sitting upright, leaning forward, and speaking in single words. The peak flow is 40% of personal best, and SpO2 is 88% after one albuterol treatment. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Give a cough suppressant and recheck in an hour
options.B: Apply oxygen and give the next ordered bronchodilator treatment
options.C: Teach the client to use the peak flow meter again as planned for the moment
options.D: Have the client lie down and rest for 30 minutes

questions.correct_text: Apply oxygen and give the next ordered bronchodilator treatment
explanation: Severe breathlessness and hypoxemia call for oxygen and repeated bronchodilator treatment.
Delay can lead to respiratory failure.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Asthma attack that is not improving

questions.question: A client weighing 190 kg is to be moved from bed to chair and is unsteady while bearing weight. Which method is safest?

options.A: A standard lift with a regular sling
options.B: A gait belt with two staff members pulling the client up
options.C: A mechanical lift with a bariatric-rated sling and enough staff
options.D: One nurse assisting the client to stand and pivot

questions.correct_text: A mechanical lift with a bariatric-rated sling and enough staff
explanation: Equipment must be rated for the client's weight, and enough staff reduces risk to client and nurses.
Manual lifting of this weight causes injury.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Moving a client with severe obesity

questions.question: Which client should the nurse assess first?

options.A: A 68-year-old with pneumonia, T 38.1 C, HR 98, RR 18, BP 124/72, alert and talking
options.B: A 74-year-old with a urinary infection, T 36.0 C, HR 104, RR 24, BP 98/58, newly drowsy
options.C: An 80-year-old on postoperative day 2 with pain 7/10, HR 92, RR 18, BP 140/84, alert
options.D: A 55-year-old with cellulitis, T 38.6 C, HR 110, RR 20, BP 130/80, alert and oriented

questions.correct_text: A 74-year-old with a urinary infection, T 36.0 C, HR 104, RR 24, BP 98/58, newly drowsy
explanation: Fast breathing, low BP, and new drowsiness suggest organ dysfunction and possible septic shock, even without fever.
Older adults often lack a fever, so the temperature misleads.
The febrile clients are alert with stable breathing and pressure.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with long-standing COPD is calm with RR 18 and SpO2 91% on 2 L/min. ABG results: pH 7.37, PaCO2 58 mm Hg, HCO3 33 mEq/L. How should the nurse interpret this?

options.A: Compensated respiratory acidosis consistent with the client's baseline
options.B: Uncompensated respiratory acidosis that needs urgent intubation now at this time
options.C: A normal ABG result that needs no further attention or follow-up
options.D: Primary metabolic alkalosis with partial respiratory compensation

questions.correct_text: Compensated respiratory acidosis consistent with the client's baseline
explanation: A high PaCO2 shows respiratory acidosis, and a raised HCO3 shows the kidneys have compensated, bringing the pH into the normal range.
A normal pH does not make the ABG normal.
Oxygen in this client is titrated to avoid removing the drive to breathe.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A nurse receives a subpoena for a client's medical record from a lawyer. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Ignore the subpoena, as the nurse is not named
options.B: Copy the record and mail it to the lawyer
options.C: Refer the request to the facility's health information or risk management department
options.D: Tell the lawyer the client's diagnosis by phone at this time

questions.correct_text: Refer the request to the facility's health information or risk management department
explanation: Release of records follows legal and policy steps handled by trained staff.
A nurse who gives out information on a request alone can breach privacy law.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client who is Muslim is fasting during daylight hours for Ramadan and declines daytime oral medications. The client has medically important twice-daily medications. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Insist on giving the daytime doses as ordered and explain the importance
options.B: Ask the provider and pharmacy to shift dose times outside the fasting hours
options.C: Crush the tablets and mix them into juice so the client does not notice
options.D: Document the refusal and skip the daytime doses without further discussion right now

questions.correct_text: Ask the provider and pharmacy to shift dose times outside the fasting hours
explanation: Religious practice is respected, and many schedules can be shifted to evening and early morning.
Insisting or skipping disregards the client's beliefs or leaves the illness untreated.
Hiding medication in food violates consent.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client receiving continuous gastric tube feedings has a gastric residual of 480 mL. The abdomen is soft, and the client has no nausea or vomiting. The facility policy is to hold feedings at 500 mL. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Hold the feeding and call the provider
options.B: Stop the feeding and start parenteral nutrition
options.C: Return the residual and continue the feeding while monitoring tolerance
options.D: Discard the residual and restart the feeding at half the rate as planned

questions.correct_text: Return the residual and continue the feeding while monitoring tolerance
explanation: The volume is below the facility limit, and the client has no sign of intolerance.
Returning the residual preserves fluid and electrolytes.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client arrives in the emergency department with a gunshot wound. What should the nurse do regarding legal duties and evidence?

options.A: Seal the clothing in plastic bags to prevent contamination of the other evidence right now
options.B: Report to law enforcement per state law and bag the clothing in paper with custody labels
options.C: Wait for the client's written consent before reporting the wound to the police
options.D: Cut through the bullet hole in the shirt to remove it and discard the clothing

questions.correct_text: Report to law enforcement per state law and bag the clothing in paper with custody labels
explanation: Many states require reporting of gunshot wounds.
Clothing is saved in paper bags, since plastic traps moisture and damages evidence, and the chain of custody is documented.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: An unconscious client has no advance directive. The daughter says, "Mom told me she would not want a feeding tube." Another family member wants the tube placed. Which principle should guide the decision?

options.A: The best-interest standard, decided by the nurse caring for the client
options.B: Placement of the tube as the default standard of care for the situation
options.C: Substituted judgment, based on what the client would have wanted
options.D: A majority vote of the adult children who are present at the bedside

questions.correct_text: Substituted judgment, based on what the client would have wanted
explanation: A surrogate decides as the client would, using known wishes and values.
Best interest applies when the client's wishes are unknown.
The nurse and the vote of relatives do not replace the client's wishes.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A nurse who has no immunity to varicella cared for a client later found to have chickenpox. What should happen?

options.A: The nurse should wear a surgical mask and continue working at this time for the moment
options.B: The nurse should be off work for one day
options.C: The nurse may work normally unless a rash appears
options.D: The nurse should be off work from about day 8 to day 21 after the exposure

questions.correct_text: The nurse should be off work from about day 8 to day 21 after the exposure
explanation: The virus can spread from a nonimmune nurse before a rash appears, starting about the eighth day.
The exposure period lasts through day 21.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A nurse interviews a 15-year-old at a clinic visit. Which approach is best?

options.A: Ask the parent to answer the sensitive questions
options.B: Interview the adolescent alone for part of the visit and use a structured tool covering home, education, activities, drugs, and sexuality
options.C: Skip questions about drugs and sexuality unless the adolescent raises them at this time
options.D: Interview the adolescent with the parent present for the whole visit

questions.correct_text: Interview the adolescent alone for part of the visit and use a structured tool covering home, education, activities, drugs, and sexuality
explanation: Adolescents give more honest answers in private, and confidentiality builds trust.
A structured tool covers risk areas in a routine way.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client receives gentamicin every 8 hours. When is the trough level drawn?

options.A: Within 30 minutes before the next dose
options.B: At the end of the day
options.C: 4 hours after the dose
options.D: 30 minutes after the dose starts

questions.correct_text: Within 30 minutes before the next dose
explanation: The trough is the lowest level and is drawn just before the next dose.
The peak is drawn about 30 minutes after the infusion ends.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client had 5 liters of fluid removed by paracentesis. An hour later, BP falls from 124/76 to 88/54, and HR rises to 112. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Give a diuretic to remove more fluid
options.B: Walk the client to improve circulation
options.C: Raise the head of the bed and encourage fluids by mouth for the moment today
options.D: Lay the client flat and monitor the blood pressure and heart rate closely

questions.correct_text: Lay the client flat and monitor the blood pressure and heart rate closely
explanation: Removing a large volume of fluid shifts fluid from the blood into the abdomen, which lowers blood pressure.
Volume expanders such as albumin may be ordered.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client weighs 70 kg and has a sodium of 154 mEq/L (normal 140). Using free water deficit = 0.6 x weight x (sodium / 140 - 1), how much water is needed to correct the deficit?
