options.C: Output is above 0.5 mL/kg/hr and is adequate for the client's size
options.D: Output reflects normal kidney concentrating ability in an older adult

questions.correct_text: Output is below 0.5 mL/kg/hr, suggesting inadequate kidney perfusion
explanation: The minimum expected output is 0.5 mL/kg/hr, or 40 mL/hr for this client.
Each hourly volume is below 40 mL, and the trend is downward.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Interpretation of falling urine output trend

questions.question: A client has pitting edema of both legs, distended neck veins, an enlarged liver, and a weight gain of 3 kg. The lungs are clear. Which type of heart failure do these findings suggest?

options.A: Right-sided heart failure, as blood is backing up into the systemic veins
options.B: Acute pulmonary edema from a failing left ventricle
options.C: Left-sided heart failure, as blood is backing up into the lungs
options.D: Pneumonia with fluid in the lungs

questions.correct_text: Right-sided heart failure, as blood is backing up into the systemic veins
explanation: Right-sided failure causes systemic congestion with edema, neck vein distention, and liver enlargement.
Left-sided failure causes crackles, dyspnea, and cough.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has pneumonia in the right lung and is hypoxemic. Which position gives the best oxygenation?

options.A: Lying on the right side, with the affected lung down
options.B: Lying on the left side, with the healthy lung down
options.C: Lying prone with the head turned to the right
options.D: Lying flat on the back with the head down

questions.correct_text: Lying on the left side, with the healthy lung down
explanation: Blood flows more to the lung that is lower, so placing the healthy lung down matches blood flow to the better air supply.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: The laboratory calls the nurse with a critical potassium of 6.6 mEq/L. Which action is correct?

options.A: Write the result, read it back to the caller, record the caller's name and time, and report it to the provider promptly
options.B: Repeat the test before reporting it to anyone
options.C: Record the value and report it at the next scheduled rounds
options.D: Ask the laboratory to fax the result and wait for the paper copy today

questions.correct_text: Write the result, read it back to the caller, record the caller's name and time, and report it to the provider promptly
explanation: A critical value needs a read-back to confirm accuracy, a record of the call, and a prompt report.
Delay can lead to fatal arrhythmia.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client who lives at high altitude has pH 7.43, PaCO2 30 mm Hg, and HCO3 20 mEq/L. How should the nurse interpret this?

options.A: Partly compensated metabolic acidosis today
options.B: Normal acid-base balance
options.C: Fully compensated respiratory alkalosis
options.D: Uncompensated respiratory alkalosis

questions.correct_text: Fully compensated respiratory alkalosis
explanation: A low PaCO2 with a pH on the alkaline side of 7.40 points to respiratory alkalosis.
A lowered bicarbonate shows the kidneys have compensated and the pH is back in range.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with a fentanyl transdermal patch develops a temperature of 39.6 C. The client's pain is 3/10 and the client is drowsy but easy to wake. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Cut the patch in half to lower the dose delivered during the fever
options.B: Monitor sedation and respiratory rate; fever can increase fentanyl absorption
options.C: Apply a heating pad over the patch to improve the client's pain control
options.D: Remove the patch and apply a new one at a different site on the chest now for the moment

questions.correct_text: Monitor sedation and respiratory rate; fever can increase fentanyl absorption
explanation: Fever raises skin blood flow and speeds drug release from the patch, which raises the risk of respiratory depression.
Heat over the patch increases absorption further, and a cut patch releases an uncontrolled dose.
A new patch adds more drug on top of the one still in the skin.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client weighing 80 kg is in septic shock. The order is 30 mL/kg of crystalloid. How many mL should be given?

options.B: 240 mL
options.D: 800 mL

questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A nurse sees a colleague give the wrong dose of insulin to a client. The client has no symptoms yet, and the colleague asks the nurse not to say anything. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Wait to see whether the client develops symptoms before deciding to report it
options.B: Ensure the client is assessed and report the error through the chain of command
options.C: Tell the colleague to fix the error quietly and say nothing to the manager
options.D: Keep quiet to protect the colleague and recheck the glucose later in the shift as planned

questions.correct_text: Ensure the client is assessed and report the error through the chain of command
explanation: The first duty is client safety, which includes assessment and treatment of any harm.
Reporting allows the system to learn and protects other clients.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Duty to report a colleague's error

questions.question: The care plan for a client with a stage 2 sacral pressure injury states, "Wound will be smaller in 7 days." After 7 days the wound is larger, repositioning every 2 hours was done as planned, and meal intake averages 30%. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Reassess the client, including nutrition, and revise the plan
options.B: Mark the outcome as met after confirming repositioning was completed
options.C: Remove the nursing diagnosis from the plan and close the problem
options.D: Continue the current plan unchanged for 7 more days and reevaluate

questions.correct_text: Reassess the client, including nutrition, and revise the plan
explanation: An unmet outcome calls for reassessment to find barriers, such as poor intake, and a revised plan.
Completing an intervention does not mean the outcome was achieved.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client had a total gastrectomy. Which teaching about long-term supplements is correct?

options.A: Vitamin B12 is needed for the first 3 months of recovery
options.B: Vitamin B12 can be taken by mouth in a daily multivitamin today
options.C: Vitamin B12 is not needed if the client eats meat
options.D: Vitamin B12 injections will be needed for life, as the stomach no longer makes intrinsic factor

questions.correct_text: Vitamin B12 injections will be needed for life, as the stomach no longer makes intrinsic factor
explanation: Intrinsic factor from the stomach is needed to absorb B12 from the gut.
Without it, the client risks pernicious anemia and nerve damage.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has a painful, punched-out ulcer on the toe, a cool pale foot, weak pulses, and pain at night that eases when the leg hangs down. What should the nurse conclude and do?

options.A: A diabetic nerve ulcer; soak the foot in hot water
options.B: Venous insufficiency; apply a tight compression wrap
options.C: Arterial insufficiency; avoid compression and keep the leg from elevation
options.D: A pressure ulcer; massage the area

questions.correct_text: Arterial insufficiency; avoid compression and keep the leg from elevation
explanation: The pain, pale skin, and weak pulses show poor blood flow to the foot.
Compression or elevation lowers flow further.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A nurse gives an IV antibiotic by rapid push. The client becomes flushed with a headache and chest tightness, and HR rises to 118. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Give acetaminophen and finish the dose
options.B: Slow the injection by half and continue for the moment
options.C: Flush with saline to dilute the drug
options.D: Stop the injection at once and assess the client

questions.correct_text: Stop the injection at once and assess the client
explanation: Rapid injection causes a sudden high drug level, known as speed shock.
The drug is stopped, and the client is assessed and monitored.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Three days after a gastrostomy tube was placed, the tube comes out. The client has no pain. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Insert a urinary catheter into the stoma to keep the tract from closing
options.B: Cover the site with a sterile dressing, keep NPO, and call the provider
options.C: Reinsert the tube into the stoma and tape it securely in place at once
options.D: Leave the site open to air and resume the feedings through the stoma

questions.correct_text: Cover the site with a sterile dressing, keep NPO, and call the provider
explanation: The tract is not yet mature and can seal or leak into the abdomen if the tube is pushed in.
A new tube is placed by the provider, and delay can close the opening.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client who is 3 weeks after a kidney transplant and takes immunosuppressants needs a roommate in a shared room. Which client is the best choice?

options.A: A client with pneumonia and a productive cough
options.B: A client with shingles lesions on the trunk
options.C: A client admitted with a hip fracture and no sign of infection
options.D: A client with watery diarrhea of unknown cause

questions.correct_text: A client admitted with a hip fracture and no sign of infection
explanation: An immunosuppressed client should be shielded from infectious contacts.
A client with a noninfectious condition is the safest choice.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: An unconscious client named a friend as the health care agent in a signed document. The client's siblings disagree with the friend's decision about a treatment. Who has the authority to decide?

options.A: The nurse caring for the client
options.B: The sibling who is closest in age to the client for the moment right now
options.C: The majority vote of the siblings
options.D: The friend named as the agent, following the client's known wishes

questions.correct_text: The friend named as the agent, following the client's known wishes
explanation: A health care agent has legal authority when the client cannot decide.
The agent applies the client's known wishes, and disputes are referred to ethics, not settled by relatives.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: At 1400 the nurse finds that 1,000 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride ordered at 125 mL/hr from 0800 has just 300 mL infused (750 mL expected). The client has heart failure. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Increase the rate to 200 mL/hr to partly catch up over the remaining hours
options.B: Increase the rate to 350 mL/hr to finish the bag at the original time
options.C: Resume the ordered rate and assess lung sounds and respiratory status
options.D: Discard the remaining fluid and request a new bag from the pharmacy

questions.correct_text: Resume the ordered rate and assess lung sounds and respiratory status
explanation: Fluid is not rushed to catch up, especially in a client with heart failure who can develop fluid overload.
The ordered rate resumes, and the client is assessed for the effect of the delay and the current volume status.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Catching up a late IV infusion

questions.question: A client reports sudden tearing pain between the shoulder blades. The blood pressure is 190/100 in the right arm and 140/80 in the left arm. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Keep the client still and quiet, monitor the pressures in both arms, and prepare for urgent imaging and blood pressure control
options.B: Have the client walk to relieve the muscle pain at this time
options.C: Apply heat to the back and recheck in an hour
options.D: Give an anticoagulant for a possible clot

questions.correct_text: Keep the client still and quiet, monitor the pressures in both arms, and prepare for urgent imaging and blood pressure control
explanation: The findings suggest a tear in the wall of the aorta, which is life-threatening.
Anticoagulants and activity can worsen the tear.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Tearing back pain with unequal arm pressures

questions.question: A client taking simvastatin drinks a large glass of grapefruit juice each morning. What should the nurse teach?

options.A: Grapefruit juice lowers the drug level and is safe
options.B: Grapefruit juice can raise the drug level and the risk of muscle damage, so it should be avoided
options.C: Grapefruit juice improves absorption and should be taken with each dose
options.D: Grapefruit juice has no effect on any drug

questions.correct_text: Grapefruit juice can raise the drug level and the risk of muscle damage, so it should be avoided
explanation: Grapefruit blocks an enzyme that breaks down the drug in the gut.
Higher levels raise the risk of muscle breakdown.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has drooping of the lower right face and a smooth right nasolabial fold, but can wrinkle the forehead on both sides. What does this suggest?

options.A: A central lesion such as a stroke
options.B: A normal variation in facial symmetry
options.C: Trigeminal neuralgia
options.D: Bell palsy, a condition that spares the lower face

questions.correct_text: A central lesion such as a stroke
explanation: The forehead has input from both sides of the brain, so a stroke spares it.
Bell palsy involves the nerve itself and weakens the forehead as well.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client weighing 70 kg has a stage 3 pressure injury. The dietitian recommends 1.25 to 1.5 g of protein per kg daily. How much protein should the client receive each day?

options.A: 56 to 70 g

explanation: Healing wounds need more protein than the usual 0.8 g/kg.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Protein needs with a pressure injury

questions.question: A client was placed in violent restraints at 0800. At 1030 the client is calm, cooperative, and apologizes. The order is valid until 1200. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Begin releasing the restraints per policy and document the criteria met
options.B: Keep the restraints on until the order expires at 1200, then reassess
options.C: Remove the restraints but skip documentation to avoid confusing the record
options.D: Wait for the provider's face-to-face evaluation before releasing the restraints

questions.correct_text: Begin releasing the restraints per policy and document the criteria met
explanation: Restraints are removed at the earliest time the behavior no longer requires them, even before the order ends.
The nurse does not need a new order to stop a restraint, and the reason is documented.
Keeping a calm client restrained without need is unlawful restriction.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Releasing restraints when criteria are met

questions.question: The pharmacy sends insulin NPH for a client's continuous IV insulin infusion order. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Start the infusion at half the ordered rate and check the glucose often
options.B: Start the infusion as sent by pharmacy and check the glucose every hour
options.C: Withhold the infusion; regular insulin is the form given IV
options.D: Dilute the NPH in saline to clear the cloudiness and start the infusion

questions.correct_text: Withhold the infusion; regular insulin is the form given IV
explanation: NPH is a suspension that is not given by vein and could cause serious harm.
Regular insulin is the form used for IV infusion.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Insulin type for an IV infusion

questions.question: A 3-year-old cried loudly when the parents left on admission. After 5 days in the hospital, the child no longer cries, plays quietly alone, and shows no reaction when the parents leave or return. How should the nurse interpret this behavior?

options.A: The protest stage of separation anxiety
options.B: Detachment, a sign of unresolved distress that needs more parent presence
options.C: Successful adjustment to the hospital routine
options.D: Normal developmental maturity for a preschooler for the moment

questions.correct_text: Detachment, a sign of unresolved distress that needs more parent presence
explanation: Detachment follows protest and despair and shows the child has given up hope of the parents' return.
It looks like calm adjustment but signals a risk to emotional bonding.
Parent presence and consistent caregivers are the main interventions.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client receiving tube feedings has had 6 watery stools daily for 2 days, abdominal cramping, and a WBC of 15,000/mm3. The client finished antibiotics 5 days ago. A PRN loperamide order is available. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Slow the feeding rate by half and observe the stool output for 24 hours
options.B: Dilute the formula by half and keep the same hourly infusion rate going
options.C: Hold the loperamide and send a stool specimen for C. difficile testing
options.D: Give the loperamide to slow the stools and reassess the output in 4 hours

questions.correct_text: Hold the loperamide and send a stool specimen for C. difficile testing
explanation: Antibiotic exposure with watery diarrhea, cramps, and a raised WBC suggests C. difficile infection.
An antidiarrheal can trap toxin in the colon, and testing guides treatment.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Diarrhea with tube feeding after antibiotics

questions.question: A nurse is about to flush a central venous catheter and has just a 3 mL syringe. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Use the 3 mL syringe and push the plunger slowly
options.B: Use a 10 mL or larger syringe, as small syringes create high pressure that can damage the catheter
options.C: Use the 3 mL syringe and push the plunger firmly to clear any clot for now
options.D: Use any needleless syringe, as the size does not matter

questions.correct_text: Use a 10 mL or larger syringe, as small syringes create high pressure that can damage the catheter
explanation: A smaller barrel produces a higher pressure for the same force and may rupture the catheter.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A child weighs 15 kg and has an order for a 20 mL/kg bolus over 15 minutes. At what rate in mL/hr should the nurse set the pump?

options.A: 300 mL/hr
options.B: 600 mL/hr
options.C: 1,200 mL/hr
options.D: 20 mL/hr

questions.correct_text: 1,200 mL/hr
explanation: Volume: 20 x 15 = 300 mL.
300 mL in 15 minutes is 1,200 mL/hr.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with psychosis says calmly, "When I leave here I'm going to hurt my neighbor. I know when she's home alone." What is the nurse's best action?

options.A: Report the statement to the provider and follow policy for warning the neighbor
options.B: Document the statement and reassess the client's mood and behavior each shift
options.C: Ask the client to promise not to harm the neighbor and document the promise
options.D: Keep the statement confidential under client privacy rules until the client acts

questions.correct_text: Report the statement to the provider and follow policy for warning the neighbor
explanation: A specific threat against an identifiable person overrides confidentiality and requires a duty-to-warn response.
A promise or routine monitoring does not protect the neighbor.
Reporting through the chain and facility policy keeps the nurse within legal duty.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: An ABG syringe has a large air bubble that remained in the sample for 10 minutes before testing. What should the nurse conclude?

options.A: The results are valid, as the sample was kept on ice the whole time
options.B: The bicarbonate is falsely high, and the others are accurate
options.C: The results are unreliable, so a new sample should be drawn
options.D: The pH is affected, but the other values can still be used safely

questions.correct_text: The results are unreliable, so a new sample should be drawn
explanation: Air exchanges gases with the blood, which raises the PaO2 and lowers the PaCO2.
A properly sealed, bubble-free sample is needed.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Air in an arterial blood gas sample

questions.question: A client with diabetes taking metoprolol reports hunger and a headache. There is no tremor, and HR is 66. The glucose is 44 mg/dL. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Treat the hypoglycemia; the beta blocker can hide tremor and a fast pulse
options.B: Recheck the glucose in 1 hour and offer a snack if the value is still low
options.C: Reassure the client, as the pulse rate is within normal limits for age
options.D: Give a PRN analgesic for the headache and recheck the client in an hour

questions.correct_text: Treat the hypoglycemia; the beta blocker can hide tremor and a fast pulse
explanation: Beta blockers blunt the usual warning signs of low glucose, so a glucose level confirms the diagnosis.
Sweating and hunger may be the only signs.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Hypoglycemia masked by a beta blocker

questions.question: A client has a shallow, irregular ankle ulcer with weeping, brown skin discoloration, and leg swelling. Pedal pulses are present, and the pain eases when the legs are raised. What should the nurse anticipate first?

options.A: Debriding the wound edges at the bedside before dressing it
options.B: Applying a warm compress to increase blood flow to the ulcer as planned
options.C: Keeping the legs in a dependent position to improve healing
options.D: Checking the ankle-brachial index before applying compression

questions.correct_text: Checking the ankle-brachial index before applying compression
explanation: The findings fit venous insufficiency, which is treated with compression and leg elevation.
Arterial flow is confirmed before compression because compression harms a leg with poor arterial supply.
A dependent position increases swelling, and heat can worsen tissue damage.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with a chest tube is being moved to radiology. Which action is correct?

options.A: Clamp the tube and place the drainage unit on the bed beside the client
options.B: Keep the system upright below the chest and leave the tubing unclamped
options.C: Raise the unit above the chest level to prevent spills during transport
options.D: Disconnect the drainage unit and cap the end of the chest tube for transport

questions.correct_text: Keep the system upright below the chest and leave the tubing unclamped
explanation: A drainage system below the chest allows air and fluid to leave the pleural space, and an unclamped tube prevents air building up.
Clamping can cause a tension pneumothorax, and a raised unit lets fluid flow back.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: While inventorying belongings, a nurse finds a handgun in a client's bag. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Leave the weapon untouched, keep others away, and contact security per policy
options.B: Leave it in the bag and document nothing
options.C: Unload the weapon and place it in a locked drawer right now
options.D: Give the bag back to the client to take home

questions.correct_text: Leave the weapon untouched, keep others away, and contact security per policy
explanation: Handling a weapon puts staff and clients at risk, and security has the training and authority to secure it.
The event is documented according to policy.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Firearm found in a client's belongings

questions.question: During wound closure, the circulating nurse finds the sponge count is one short. The surgeon wants to close. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Ask the scrub person to sign the count sheet as correct and proceed
options.B: Inform the surgeon, recount, and obtain imaging per policy before closure
options.C: Allow closure and request an x-ray after the client leaves the room
options.D: Document the discrepancy and allow the closure to continue as planned for the moment

questions.correct_text: Inform the surgeon, recount, and obtain imaging per policy before closure
explanation: A retained sponge is a preventable never event, so the count must be resolved before the cavity is closed.
Documentation or later imaging allows a retained item to remain unnoticed.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A toddler drank a small amount of bleach and is crying but breathing easily. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Give syrup of ipecac to make the child bring the bleach back up
options.B: Give diluted vinegar to neutralize the bleach in the child's stomach
options.C: Give a large volume of milk and wait to see if symptoms appear
options.D: Avoid inducing vomiting, rinse the mouth, and call poison control

questions.correct_text: Avoid inducing vomiting, rinse the mouth, and call poison control
explanation: Vomiting causes a second burn of the throat and risks aspiration.
Neutralizing agents produce heat and more injury.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with a history of substance use has a fresh surgical incision and requests the PRN opioid every 3 hours. The client is wincing, with HR 108. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Assess the pain objectively and give the medication per the order
options.B: Delay the dose, as the client is probably seeking drugs
options.C: Document drug-seeking behavior and withhold the dose
options.D: Give a non-opioid in place of the opioid, given the history right now

questions.correct_text: Assess the pain objectively and give the medication per the order
explanation: A history of substance use does not remove the right to pain relief.
Objective signs and an incision support true pain.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A nurse with no known TB exposure and no BCG vaccine has a Mantoux test read at 48 hours. The site shows 12 mm of induration and 25 mm of redness. How should the result be interpreted?

options.A: Negative; induration must reach 15 mm or more in a healthcare worker
options.B: Positive; induration of 10 mm or more is positive in a healthcare worker
options.C: Invalid; the test result must be read at 72 hours and the site remeasured
options.D: Negative; the surrounding redness must exceed 30 mm to be considered positive

questions.correct_text: Positive; induration of 10 mm or more is positive in a healthcare worker
explanation: Only induration is measured, not redness.
The positive cutoff depends on risk; 10 mm or more is positive for healthcare workers.
Reading between 48 and 72 hours is valid.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client takes an ACE inhibitor and a diuretic, and starts ibuprofen for back pain. After 3 days, the creatinine has doubled, and urine output is low. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Acute kidney injury from the combined effect of the drugs
options.B: A normal response to a new pain medicine
options.C: An effect of the back pain on the kidneys
options.D: A reaction to the client's usual diet

questions.correct_text: Acute kidney injury from the combined effect of the drugs
explanation: The combination reduces blood flow to the kidneys and can cause injury.
The NSAID is stopped, and the provider evaluates the client.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Combined drugs that harm the kidneys

questions.question: A client with liver disease has a total calcium of 7.4 mg/dL and an albumin of 2.0 g/dL. The client has no tingling, muscle spasms, or ECG changes. How should the nurse interpret the result?

options.A: The client has true hypocalcemia and should receive IV calcium gluconate immediately
options.B: The corrected calcium is near normal; the low total value mostly reflects low albumin
options.C: The result is unreliable and the albumin level should be repeated before any action
options.D: The client is at risk for tetany and seizure precautions should begin on the unit now

questions.correct_text: The corrected calcium is near normal; the low total value mostly reflects low albumin
explanation: Corrected calcium is about 7.4 + 0.8 x (4.0 - 2.0) = 9.0 mg/dL, within the normal range.
Low albumin lowers total calcium without lowering the active (ionized) fraction, and the client has no symptoms.
An ionized calcium level would confirm if doubt remains.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has a gastrostomy tube. Four oral medication orders are written. Which order should the nurse question?

options.A: Furosemide immediate-release tablet 40 mg crushed by tube daily
options.B: Acetaminophen liquid 650 mg by tube every 6 hours as needed
options.C: Famotidine immediate-release tablet 20 mg crushed by tube twice daily right now
options.D: Oxycodone extended-release tablet 20 mg crushed by tube every 12 hours

questions.correct_text: Oxycodone extended-release tablet 20 mg crushed by tube every 12 hours
explanation: Crushing an extended-release tablet releases the entire dose at once, which can cause overdose and respiratory depression.
Liquids and plain immediate-release tablets can be given through a tube after crushing and dissolving.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Crushing medications for a feeding tube

questions.question: A competent client says, "I stopped taking my blood pressure pills. Please don't tell the doctor." What should the nurse do?

options.A: Tell the client to restart the pills and not mention it again
options.B: Document nothing, as the client has the right to refuse medication today
options.C: Explain that the information affects safe care and must be shared with the team, while exploring the client's reasons
options.D: Promise to keep the secret to preserve the client's trust

questions.correct_text: Explain that the information affects safe care and must be shared with the team, while exploring the client's reasons
explanation: The treatment team needs accurate information, and confidentiality does not prevent sharing within the team.
Understanding why the client stopped helps solve the problem.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Client's secret about stopping a medication

questions.question: A client 1 day after abdominal surgery has a mildly distended abdomen. The nurse hears no bowel sounds in the right lower quadrant after 30 seconds. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Keep listening in that quadrant for up to 5 minutes and compare the four quadrants
options.B: Insert a nasogastric tube per protocol to decompress the distended abdomen
options.C: Document a paralytic ileus and ask about starting bowel stimulants today
options.D: Document absent bowel sounds in that quadrant and keep the client NPO tonight at this time

questions.correct_text: Keep listening in that quadrant for up to 5 minutes and compare the four quadrants
explanation: Bowel sounds must be listened for up to 5 minutes in a quadrant before they are called absent.
Reduced sounds are common in the first postoperative days from anesthesia and handling of the bowel.
Labeling an ileus on one quiet quadrant is premature.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client received 3 liters of IV fluid over 8 hours. The hematocrit is now 35%, down from 45%. Vital signs are stable, and there is no sign of bleeding. How should the nurse interpret this?

options.A: Acute hemorrhage that needs an immediate transfusion of red cells now right now
options.B: Dehydration that needs more IV fluid and a repeat hematocrit tomorrow
options.C: Chronic anemia from poor intake that needs iron therapy and referral
options.D: Hemodilution from the fluid; follow the trend with the clinical status

questions.correct_text: Hemodilution from the fluid; follow the trend with the clinical status
explanation: Added plasma volume dilutes the red cell concentration without a loss of cells.
Stable vital signs and no bleeding support dilution, and the trend is rechecked.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A woman with a wrist fracture and bruises on her trunk is accompanied by her partner, who answers every question. She avoids eye contact. Which approach is best for screening?

options.A: Ask the partner to describe how the injuries happened and compare the stories
options.B: Separate her from the partner for a routine test and screen privately
options.C: Leave a hotline brochure and a pamphlet on the bedside table to read later
options.D: Ask about safety at home while the partner remains at the bedside to help

questions.correct_text: Separate her from the partner for a routine test and screen privately
explanation: Screening is done privately, and a routine reason to separate the couple does not alert the partner.
Asking in front of the partner endangers her, and a brochure left in view can lead to harm.
The partner's account is unreliable if he is the source of the injuries.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Which medication order is written in the safest format?

options.A: Hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV q4h PRN pain, MS if no relief
options.B: Hydromorphone .5 mg IV every 4 hours as needed for pain
options.C: Hydromorphone 2.0 mg IV every 4 hours as needed for pain
options.D: Hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV every 4 hours as needed for pain

questions.correct_text: Hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV every 4 hours as needed for pain
explanation: A leading zero before a decimal prevents a missed decimal point from causing a tenfold overdose.
A trailing zero (2.0) can be misread as 20, and the order with ".5" lacks a leading zero.
The last order uses an error-prone abbreviation ("MS") that could mean morphine or magnesium sulfate.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing
questions.topic: Safe format of a medication order

questions.question: A client with diabetes and peripheral artery disease has a dry, black, intact eschar on the heel with no redness, swelling, or drainage. No debridement is ordered. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Apply wet-to-dry dressings twice daily to loosen and remove the eschar
options.B: Keep the area dry and intact, offload the heel, and monitor for signs of infection
options.C: Apply a moist hydrogel dressing daily to soften the eschar for later removal
options.D: Scrub the eschar gently with saline gauze at each dressing change to remove it for the moment

questions.correct_text: Keep the area dry and intact, offload the heel, and monitor for signs of infection
explanation: Stable dry eschar acts as a natural cover over an ischemic wound and is left in place without debridement.
Moisture and removal risk infection and tissue loss in a limb with poor blood flow.
Offloading and watching for infection signs are the priorities.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has a cardiac output of 5.4 L/min and a heart rate of 90/min. What is the stroke volume?

options.A: 60 mL
options.B: 5.4 mL
options.D: 486 mL

questions.correct_text: 60 mL
explanation: Stroke volume = cardiac output / heart rate.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with cirrhosis and ascites has new orders. Which order should the nurse question?

options.A: Furosemide 40 mg by mouth every morning with daily weights
options.B: Acetaminophen 1,000 mg by mouth every 4 hours around the clock
options.C: Lactulose 30 mL by mouth twice daily with a goal of two to three soft stools
options.D: A 2-gram sodium restriction with a review by the dietitian

questions.correct_text: Acetaminophen 1,000 mg by mouth every 4 hours around the clock
explanation: A damaged liver clears acetaminophen poorly, and this order would give 6,000 mg a day.
Lactulose, a diuretic with weights, and sodium restriction are standard care.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client on bed rest has a purple-maroon, intact, boggy area on the heel that is painful and warmer than the surrounding skin. What should the nurse conclude and do?

options.A: Stage 1 injury; massage the area to improve circulation
options.B: Stage 2 injury; remove the blister roof and apply a dressing
options.C: Unstageable injury; apply a hydrocolloid dressing and leave it for 5 days for the moment
options.D: Deep tissue injury; offload pressure from the heel and monitor how it evolves

questions.correct_text: Deep tissue injury; offload pressure from the heel and monitor how it evolves
explanation: Purple-maroon discoloration of intact skin with pain and a boggy feel suggests damage to deeper tissue.
The injury can evolve into a full-thickness wound, so pressure is removed completely and the area is watched.
Massage damages already injured tissue.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A trauma client has received 10 units of red cells in 2 hours and now reports tingling and muscle cramps. The ECG shows a prolonged QT interval. What does the nurse suspect?

options.A: Low calcium from citrate in the stored blood
options.B: High potassium from leakage out of stored red blood cells
options.C: Low sodium from dilution by the transfused volume
options.D: Low magnesium from poor nutrition before the injury

questions.correct_text: Low calcium from citrate in the stored blood
explanation: Citrate binds calcium, and large volumes can drop the level fast.
Tingling, cramps, and a prolonged QT interval fit low calcium.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: In a client's left ear, bone conduction is heard longer than air conduction (Rinne test), and the sound in the Weber test is heard louder in the left ear. What do these results suggest?

options.A: Normal hearing in both ears
options.B: A sensorineural hearing loss in the left ear
options.C: A conductive hearing loss in the left ear
options.D: A sensorineural hearing loss in the right ear

questions.correct_text: A conductive hearing loss in the left ear
explanation: In conductive loss, air conduction falls below bone conduction and the Weber sound lateralizes to the affected ear.
In sensorineural loss, the sound goes to the better ear.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client has these Braden subscale scores: sensory perception 3, moisture 2, activity 2, mobility 2, nutrition 2, and friction and shear 2. What is the total score and risk level?

options.A: 15; mild risk
options.B: 13; low risk
options.C: 11; very high risk
options.D: 13; moderate risk

questions.correct_text: 13; moderate risk
explanation: The total is 3 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 13.
A score of 13 to 14 is moderate risk, and 12 or below is high risk.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: An electronic record lets a nurse copy the previous shift's assessment forward. The nurse is busy and the client looks unchanged. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Copy the entry forward, as the client appears unchanged
options.B: Copy the entry forward and change just the time
options.C: Perform and document a new assessment for the current shift
options.D: Ask the previous nurse to confirm the assessment by phone right now

questions.correct_text: Perform and document a new assessment for the current shift
explanation: A chart entry must reflect what the nurse found, and a copied entry can carry forward errors.
Each shift documents its own data.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client with long-term alcohol use is confused and has a glucose of 38 mg/dL. IV 50% dextrose and thiamine are both ordered. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Give the dextrose alone, as thiamine does not affect the outcome
options.B: Give the thiamine before or with the dextrose
options.C: Hold both until the glucose is repeated in an hour
options.D: Give the dextrose first and the thiamine at the next scheduled time

questions.correct_text: Give the thiamine before or with the dextrose
explanation: A sugar load in a thiamine-deficient client can trigger Wernicke encephalopathy.
The low glucose still needs treatment without delay.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A client arrives with a knife impaled in the thigh. Bleeding is moderate. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Cut the object off at the skin and discard it
options.B: Remove the object and apply direct pressure to the site today
options.C: Stabilize the object in place and control bleeding around it
options.D: Pull the object out slowly in the direction it entered

questions.correct_text: Stabilize the object in place and control bleeding around it
explanation: The object may be pressing on a vessel, and removal can cause massive bleeding.
It is secured in place and removed under controlled conditions.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: A nurse inserts a small-bore feeding tube for a client taking a proton pump inhibitor. The aspirate pH is 6, and the client is not coughing. What should the nurse do before starting the feeding?

options.A: Inject 20 mL of air and listen over the stomach
options.B: Document placement as confirmed by pH
options.C: Start the feeding slowly and watch for coughing
options.D: Obtain an x-ray to confirm tube placement

questions.correct_text: Obtain an x-ray to confirm tube placement
explanation: A pH of 5 or less supports gastric placement, but acid suppression raises gastric pH and makes the value unreliable.
Air auscultation cannot tell stomach from lung, and a client without a cough can still have a misplaced tube.
A new small-bore tube needs radiographic confirmation.
questions.subject: Foundation of Nursing

questions.question: Order: acetaminophen 15 mg/kg by mouth. The child weighs 12 kg. Available: 160 mg/5 mL. How many mL should the nurse give? (Round to the nearest tenth.)

options.B: 5.6 mL
options.C: 2.8 mL
options.D: 4.5 mL

options.B: 85; high risk
options.C: 70; high risk

options.A: IV calcium

questions.correct_text: IV calcium

questions.question: During endotracheal suctioning, a client's heart rate falls from 82 to 48 with new ventricular ectopy, and SpO2 is 85%. What should the nurse do?

options.B: Stop suctioning and give 100% oxygen
options.C: Increase the suction pressure to finish faster
options.D: Instill saline and continue suctioning

questions.correct_text: Stop suctioning and give 100% oxygen

Oxygen is given and the client is monitored until stable.
